Lulu.escape: Your chance to attack comes after Lulu W Whimsy is used on another ally. Lulu has no dash to escape on her own, so if you land Xerath E Shocking Orb while keeping your distance then, it's easy to follow up. You also have no escape ability, so check your own safety before using E.
Lulu.fight: Since Lulu can absorb heavy damage with a shield, keep up steady poke by slowing her with Xerath W Eye of Destruction, then firing Xerath Q Arcanopulse, instead of unloading everything at once. If Lulu W Whimsy is used on another ally and Lulu E Help, Pix!'s shield is also on an ally, look for Xerath E Shocking Orb from an angle where minions won't block it.
Lulu.build: Early on, buy a Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Lulu deals mostly magic damage and Xerath tends to have low magic resistance, so prioritize magic resistance.
Lulu.combo: For a kill attempt, stun with Xerath E Shocking Orb from an angle where minions won't block it, hit the center of Xerath W Eye of Destruction, then follow with Xerath Q Arcanopulse. If E misses, stop the combo and save your mana. For regular poke, hit with W's slow first, then fire Q.
Lulu.laning: Stand behind minions to reduce the extra damage from Lulu P Pix, Faerie Companion, and use your range advantage to poke with Xerath Q Arcanopulse. Don't push the wave unnecessarily; if you need to push, secure river vision first. Fire Q only when you have a good angle so you don't run low on mana, and use Xerath P Mana Surge when it's safe.
Lulu.phase: In the late game, a positioning mistake can get you caught immediately, so fight from a safe distance.
Lulu.teamfight: Start from the far back and deal damage with Xerath W Eye of Destruction and Xerath R Rite of the Arcane after your allies lock down the enemy. If Lulu R Wild Growth is available, don't focus only on the target she would protect; go for Lulu herself or someone else. Save Xerath E Shocking Orb to stop enemies who get on you, and cast R from a safe position.
Lulu.watch: If you are hit by Lulu W Whimsy, you are silenced and may lose the chance to protect yourself with Xerath E Shocking Orb, so keep your distance. Lulu R Wild Growth immediately increases its target's health and knocks up nearby enemies, so don't commit your abilities expecting a kill on a target while R is available.

Heimerdinger.laning: Poke with the range of Xerath Q Arcanopulse from behind minions, but don’t push the lane unless you need to. If you need to push, secure river vision first, then fire Xerath Q Arcanopulse when your opponent steps forward to last-hit. If your aim is off, cancel the charge to save mana; when it’s safe, use basic attacks to trigger Xerath P Mana Surge.
Heimerdinger.build: Buy Null-Magic Mantle first in the early game, and choose Mercury’s Treads for boots. Heimerdinger’s main damage is magic, and Xerath has relatively low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first.
Heimerdinger.combo: When you have a chance to kill, stun him with Xerath E Shocking Orb from an angle that minions won’t block, hit the center of Xerath W Eye of Destruction, then follow with Xerath Q Arcanopulse. If Xerath E Shocking Orb misses, save your follow-up spells. For regular poke, slow him first with Xerath W Eye of Destruction, then fire Xerath Q Arcanopulse.
Heimerdinger.escape: Heimerdinger has no ability to create distance on his own, so landing Xerath E Shocking Orb then makes it easy to follow up with more attacks. Also look for openings just after a turret is placed or just after it finishes a powerful shot.
Heimerdinger.fight: Push Heimerdinger himself back while keeping your distance instead of trading head-on in front of his turrets. When you have an opening to approach, cast Xerath E Shocking Orb so it isn’t blocked by minions and lock him down.
Heimerdinger.phase: In the late game, a poor position makes you easy to catch, so secure a safe position first.
Heimerdinger.teamfight: Start from the far back, and deal damage with Xerath W Eye of Destruction and Xerath R Rite of the Arcane after your team locks down an enemy. Save Xerath E Shocking Orb to interrupt anyone who gets on top of you. When Heimerdinger R UPGRADE!!! is available, don’t group up in a narrow area around an objective; from a safe position, poke enemies during the standoff with Xerath Q Arcanopulse.
Heimerdinger.watch: If you get hit, immediately leave turret range.

Brand.phase: In the late game, poor positioning can get you killed instantly, so stay back and watch Brand’s area damage range and your spacing from allies.
Brand.build: Buy a Null-Magic Mantle first in the early game, and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Brand’s damage is mainly magic, so build magic resistance first. Xerath’s damage is also mainly magic, and Brand tends to have low magic resistance.
Brand.combo: The reliable combo is to stun with Xerath E Shocking Orb, hit the center of Xerath W Eye of Destruction, then cast Xerath Q Arcanopulse. If Xerath E Shocking Orb misses, don’t continue the combo; save your mana. Try it while Brand W Pillar of Flame is down, from an angle where Xerath E Shocking Orb won’t be blocked by minions.
Brand.escape: The moment Brand W Pillar of Flame is down is your chance to close the distance. If you’re on fire, first avoid the stun risk from Brand Q Sear, then catch Brand with Xerath E Shocking Orb when you’re no longer burning. Brand has no ability to create distance on his own, but if Xerath E Shocking Orb misses as you engage, don’t push further.
Brand.fight: For poke when you don’t have a kill opportunity, hit the center of Xerath W Eye of Destruction to slow Brand, then follow with Xerath Q Arcanopulse. Look for a chance to close the distance and stun him with Xerath E Shocking Orb when Brand W Pillar of Flame is down and Brand P Blaze isn’t applied. If Brand Q Sear is available and you’re on fire, dodge the projectile first.
Brand.laning: Poke with Xerath Q Arcanopulse from behind minions, but don’t push the lane unnecessarily. Don’t last-hit next to minions Brand has set on fire, and step to the side when the wave is clustered. Save mana early by casting only when you have a spot to hit, and use basic attacks to trigger Xerath P Mana Surge when it’s safe.
Brand.teamfight: Start from the back and deal damage with Xerath W Eye of Destruction and Xerath R Rite of the Arcane after your allies lock down the enemy. Brand E Conflagration spreads around burning targets and Brand R Pyroclasm bounces between enemies, so don’t stand next to a burning ally. Use Xerath R Rite of the Arcane from a safe position and save Xerath E Shocking Orb to interrupt anyone who gets on top of you.
Brand.watch: Dodge Brand W Pillar of Flame and Brand Q Sear first to make it easier to prevent Brand P Blaze stacks and the explosion. If you’re on fire, go behind minions or move out of Brand Q Sear’s projectile path to avoid the stun. When you see Brand R Pyroclasm being cast, spread out from allies.

Ahri.build: Buy Null-Magic Mantle early to survive, and choose Mercury’s Treads for boots. Since most of Ahri’s damage is magic, build magic resistance first, but magic resistance cannot reduce the true damage from Ahri Q Orb of Deception on its return. If the enemy has an engage assassin, buy Zhonya’s Hourglass earlier to prepare for being caught after Xerath E Shocking Orb is down.
Ahri.laning: Dodge Ahri E Charm from behind minions and poke with Xerath Q Arcanopulse at its range; there’s no need to push the lane. Look for Xerath Q Arcanopulse when Ahri steps forward to last-hit, but cancel it if the angle is off. If you need to push, get river vision first, then use Xerath P Mana Surge when it’s safe.
Ahri.combo: Stun with Xerath E Shocking Orb, hit the center of Xerath W Eye of Destruction, then fire Xerath Q Arcanopulse. Look for this sequence after dodging Ahri E Charm and while Ahri R Spirit Rush is down; don’t follow up if Xerath E Shocking Orb is blocked by minions or misses. For light poke, slow her with Xerath W Eye of Destruction, then fire Xerath Q Arcanopulse.
Ahri.escape: The moment after you dodge Ahri E Charm is an opportunity to attack. If Ahri R Spirit Rush is still available, save Xerath E Shocking Orb to stop her engage.
Ahri.fight: For trades when you aren’t going for a kill, slow Ahri by hitting the center of Xerath W Eye of Destruction, then follow with Xerath Q Arcanopulse. After dodging Ahri E Charm and while Ahri R Spirit Rush is down, look to stun with Xerath E Shocking Orb from an angle that minions won’t block. If Xerath E Shocking Orb misses, stop the follow-up combo and save mana.
Ahri.phase: In the late game, a poor position can let enemies engage and take you down immediately, so secure a safe position first.
Ahri.teamfight: Start from the very back. After your allies lock down an enemy, deal damage with Xerath W Eye of Destruction and Xerath R Rite of the Arcane. Save Xerath E Shocking Orb to stop anyone engaging on you. During sieges or standoffs around objectives, pressure with Xerath Q Arcanopulse from beyond a wall or behind a turret.
Ahri.watch: If Ahri E Charm hits you, the follow-up combo is dangerous, so dodge it with minions between you. Ahri Q Orb of Deception can hit on its return, and its return damage is true damage, so after dodging the first pass, move out of its return path too. While Ahri R Spirit Rush is available, don’t charge Xerath Q Arcanopulse for too long or cast Xerath R Rite of the Arcane from an unsafe position.

Akali.teamfight: Start from the backline and save Xerath E Shocking Orb to stop Akali’s engage. When your allies lock down an enemy, deal damage with Xerath W Eye of Destruction and Xerath R Rite of the Arcane. Xerath R Rite of the Arcane prevents you from moving while casting, so secure a safe position before using it.
Akali.build: Buy Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury’s Treads for boots early. Build magic resistance against Akali’s damage, and rush Zhonya’s Hourglass if the risk of being engaged on is high. Akali tends to have high magic resistance, so include penetration in Xerath’s build.
Akali.combo: When you have a kill opportunity, stun with Xerath E Shocking Orb, hit the center of Xerath W Eye of Destruction, then finish with Xerath Q Arcanopulse. If Xerath E Shocking Orb misses, stop the combo and save mana. For regular poke, slow her with Xerath W Eye of Destruction, then fire Xerath Q Arcanopulse.
Akali.escape: Don’t move forward just because Akali W Twilight Shroud and Akali E Shuriken Flip are down. Look for a window before Akali R Perfect Execution comes back up, hit her with Xerath E Shocking Orb to lock down her movement, then attack. If you dodged the first shuriken from Akali E Shuriken Flip, she has one fewer way to close the gap.
Akali.fight: Instead of fighting Akali up close, poke only when you can hit her from outside her range. When she comes out of Akali W Twilight Shroud to attack, stop her engage with Xerath E Shocking Orb and counterattack. If Xerath E Shocking Orb is down, don’t force the fight.
Akali.laning: Poke with Xerath Q Arcanopulse from behind minions, but don’t push the wave unnecessarily. If you have to push, secure river vision first. Save mana by firing when Akali steps forward to last-hit, and use Xerath P Mana Surge when it’s safe.
Akali.phase: In the late game, watch for Akali’s engage and be especially careful with your positioning.
Akali.watch: Prioritize dodging the first shuriken from Akali E Shuriken Flip. If its mark hits you, the second dash will follow Xerath as he retreats. You can’t dodge the first dash of Akali R Perfect Execution by walking, so save Xerath E Shocking Orb to interrupt her engage.

AurelionSol.combo: When Aurelion Sol W Astral Flight is down, stun him with Xerath E Shocking Orb, hit the center of Xerath W Eye of Destruction, then follow with Xerath Q Arcanopulse. If Xerath E Shocking Orb misses, don’t continue the combo; save your mana. Use Xerath R Rite of the Arcane after securing a safe position and locking down your opponent.
AurelionSol.build: Buy a Null-Magic Mantle first in the early game, and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Aurelion Sol’s main damage is magic, so build magic resistance first. Aurelion Sol Q Breath of Light scales with your maximum health, so don’t rely on stacking health alone.
AurelionSol.escape: The moment after you force Aurelion Sol to use W Astral Flight, his mobility tool, is your chance to close the distance and counterattack. If you stun him with Xerath E Shocking Orb then, it’s hard for Aurelion Sol to escape. If you’re caught in Aurelion Sol E Singularity, move outside immediately instead of continuing to attack.
AurelionSol.fight: Keep your distance while Aurelion Sol W Astral Flight is available, and save Xerath E Shocking Orb to interrupt his engage. After Aurelion Sol W Astral Flight is used, stun him with Xerath E Shocking Orb from an angle that isn’t blocked by minions, then counterattack. For poke when you don’t have a kill opportunity, slow him with Xerath W Eye of Destruction, then hit Xerath Q Arcanopulse.
AurelionSol.laning: Early on, poke from behind minions and use your range advantage, but cast Xerath Q Arcanopulse only when you can hit so you don’t run low on mana. You don’t need to push the lane; if you do, get river vision first. Quickly move out of Aurelion Sol Q Breath of Light’s targeting line so you don’t keep taking it and letting him stack Stardust.
AurelionSol.phase: Mid game is Xerath’s strong point once he has ability power and mana, so use your range and the pressure from Xerath R Rite of the Arcane. In the late game, watch for Aurelion Sol’s permanent scaling and empowered area-of-effect abilities, and secure a safe position first.
AurelionSol.teamfight: Start from the back and deal damage with Xerath W Eye of Destruction and Xerath R Rite of the Arcane after your allies lock down the enemy. Save Xerath E Shocking Orb to interrupt anyone who engages on you. Spread out from allies so you aren’t all caught in Aurelion Sol R Falling Star / The Skies Descend’s area effect, and don’t bunch up in narrow passages.
AurelionSol.watch: Aurelion Sol Q Breath of Light deals damage based on your maximum health, so stay behind minions and move out of its targeting line as soon as it catches you. If you’re caught in Aurelion Sol E Singularity, walk out immediately, and avoid even the edge when your health is low. Once Aurelion Sol R Falling Star / The Skies Descend is empowered, spread out from allies to avoid the area-of-effect knock-up.

Senna.phase: In the late game, watch out for the range of a scaled Senna, and have Xerath secure a safe position first.
Senna.build: In the early game, buy Cloth Armor first and choose Plated Steelcaps for your boots. Senna’s main damage is physical, so build armor first.
Senna.combo: Stun Senna with Xerath E Shocking Orb, hit the center of Xerath W Eye of Destruction, then follow with Xerath Q Arcanopulse. If Xerath E Shocking Orb misses, stop the combo and save your mana.
Senna.escape: You have a chance to close the gap after Senna W Last Embrace misses or is blocked by a minion. Senna has no ability to create distance on her own, so if you get a safe angle, stun her with Xerath E Shocking Orb and hold her there.
Senna.fight: For trades that aren’t kill attempts, slow Senna with the center of Xerath W Eye of Destruction, then hit her with Xerath Q Arcanopulse. Look for the moment Senna steps forward to collect a soul, but use Xerath E Shocking Orb carefully so you can protect yourself when Senna approaches.
Senna.laning: Watch the soul locations and poke Senna when she steps forward to collect one, disrupting her collection. Stand behind minions, but avoid the line where Senna Q Piercing Darkness passes through them. Don’t push the lane without a reason; if you have to, secure river vision first.
Senna.teamfight: Start from the back line. If Senna E Curse of the Black Mist appears, back off to secure vision, or use Xerath W Eye of Destruction and Xerath R Rite of the Arcane inside the mist to block approaches. Deal damage after your allies lock down an enemy, and save Xerath E Shocking Orb to stop enemies who get on top of you.
Senna.watch: Senna W Last Embrace is blocked by minions, so dodge it from behind your minions. If it hits you, move away from your allies before the root spreads. Get out of the straight line of Senna Q Piercing Darkness, and if it hits you once, back off so you don’t take a second hit.

Thresh.laning: Poke with Xerath Q Arcanopulse from behind minions; there’s no need to push the lane. Thresh looks for Thresh Q Death Sentence when you step up to last-hit, so change direction then. If the angle for a poke is off, cancel Xerath Q Arcanopulse to save mana. If you need to push, get river vision first.
Thresh.build: Survive the early game with Null-Magic Mantle, and choose Mercury’s Treads for your boots. Thresh’s main damage is magic, so build magic resistance first, but tenacity is more urgent for immobile Xerath to withstand Thresh’s crowd control.
Thresh.combo: For a kill, stun with Xerath E Shocking Orb, hit the center of Xerath W Eye of Destruction, then follow with Xerath Q Arcanopulse. If Xerath E Shocking Orb misses, stop the combo to save mana. For light harass, slow Thresh with Xerath W Eye of Destruction first, then cast Xerath Q Arcanopulse.
Thresh.escape: Right after dodging Thresh Q Death Sentence sideways is your chance to close the gap. Check that Thresh W Dark Passage is still on cooldown, then land Xerath E Shocking Orb to keep him from escaping.
Thresh.fight: When Thresh steps forward to collect souls, hit the center of Xerath W Eye of Destruction and cast Xerath Q Arcanopulse on the slowed target. Right after dodging Thresh Q Death Sentence is your chance to close the gap, but don’t go in recklessly if Thresh W Dark Passage is still available.
Thresh.phase: In the late game, getting engaged on is dangerous, so secure the safest position first. Harass Thresh when he steps out to collect souls so he can’t gather them freely.
Thresh.teamfight: Start from the backline and deal damage with Xerath W Eye of Destruction and Xerath R Rite of the Arcane after your allies lock down an opponent. Save Xerath E Shocking Orb to stop enemies who get on top of you. Since you can’t move during Xerath R Rite of the Arcane, find a safe position before using it. When Thresh W Dark Passage appears, use your finisher immediately or retreat; if you’re caught in Thresh R The Box, decide at once which direction to break through.
Thresh.watch: Thresh Q Death Sentence is dangerous because a hit stuns you and lets him follow up with a dash. Move sideways when you see him ready his hook, and change direction again when stepping up for a last hit. Avoid the line between Thresh and his allies so Thresh E Flay can’t pull you toward an allied side.

Akshan.build: Akshan’s main damage is physical, and Xerath has low armor, so build armor first. Buy Cloth Armor early to survive, and choose Plated Steelcaps for boots. If Akshan’s engage is a threat, rush Zhonya’s Hourglass to prepare for when Xerath E Shocking Orb is down.
Akshan.combo: If Akshan E Heroic Swing is down and you have an angle that minions won’t block, stun him with Xerath E Shocking Orb. If Xerath E Shocking Orb misses, don’t continue the combo; save mana.
Akshan.escape: Right after Akshan uses E Heroic Swing, there’s a window to close the gap or catch him. If Xerath E Shocking Orb hits then, Akshan can’t escape with a mobility ability, so use it from an angle that minions won’t block. If Xerath E Shocking Orb is down, it’s hard to respond to Akshan’s dash, so don’t engage first.
Akshan.fight: While Akshan E Heroic Swing is available, save Xerath E Shocking Orb to respond to his engage. Right after Akshan uses E, look for a window when he has no mobility and stun him with Xerath E Shocking Orb from an angle that minions won’t block. For poke when you aren’t going for a kill, slow him with Xerath W Eye of Destruction, then fire Xerath Q Arcanopulse.
Akshan.laning: Akshan Q Avengerang travels farther each time it hits a minion, so watch its outbound and return paths even when standing behind minions. Don’t push the wave unnecessarily; poke with Xerath Q Arcanopulse only when you can hit him, and secure river vision first if you need to push.
Akshan.phase: In the late game, letting enemies engage puts Xerath at risk, so focus on positioning and saving Xerath E Shocking Orb.
Akshan.teamfight: Start from the very back. After your allies lock down an enemy, deal damage with Xerath W Eye of Destruction and Xerath R Rite of the Arcane, and save Xerath E Shocking Orb to stop Akshan E Heroic Swing. Xerath R Rite of the Arcane prevents you from moving while casting, so secure a safe position before using it. If you have the Scoundrel mark, don’t face Akshan alone; fight from outside his finishing range.
Akshan.watch: Akshan Q Avengerang gains range each time it hits a minion, so don’t assume you’re safe behind minions; dodge both its outbound and return paths. If Akshan dashes along a wall with Akshan E Heroic Swing, save Xerath E Shocking Orb to stop his engage. When you’re low and the targeting indicator for Akshan R Comeuppance appears, move behind terrain instead of fleeing alone through the open.

Alistar.build: Buy Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury’s Treads for boots early. Alistar’s main damage is magic, and Xerath has relatively low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first.
Alistar.combo: After Alistar W Headbutt is down, stun him with Xerath E Shocking Orb, hit the center of Xerath W Eye of Destruction, then fire Xerath Q Arcanopulse. If Xerath E Shocking Orb misses, don’t continue the combo; save mana. For light poke, slow him with Xerath W Eye of Destruction, then fire Xerath Q Arcanopulse.
Alistar.escape: Only close the gap to counterattack right after Alistar W Headbutt and Alistar Q Pulverize are down. Bait out Alistar W Headbutt, then hit him with Xerath E Shocking Orb to create a window where he can’t escape.
Alistar.fight: For poke when you aren’t going for a kill, slow Alistar by hitting the center of Xerath W Eye of Destruction, then fire Xerath Q Arcanopulse. If Alistar W Headbutt and Alistar Q Pulverize are down, reposition and counterattack. While Alistar R Unbreakable Will is active, don’t unload your abilities; back off and fight again afterward.
Alistar.laning: Poke with Xerath Q Arcanopulse from behind minions, but don’t push the wave unnecessarily. Xerath E Shocking Orb is blocked by minions, so keep an angle open to respond to Alistar’s engage. Mana is scarce early, so fire Xerath Q Arcanopulse only when you have a position to hit; cancel it if the angle is off.
Alistar.phase: Early on, Xerath is fragile and uses a lot of mana, so avoid Alistar’s engage and limit how often you poke. In the late game, one positioning mistake can get you caught, so keep a safe distance.
Alistar.teamfight: Start from the very back. After your allies lock down an enemy, target the backline carries with Xerath W Eye of Destruction and Xerath R Rite of the Arcane. Don’t spend your damage on Alistar while Alistar R Unbreakable Will is active.
Alistar.watch: If Alistar closes the gap with Alistar W Headbutt, he can follow with the knock-up from Alistar Q Pulverize and the stun from Alistar E Trample, so keep your distance first. Save Xerath E Shocking Orb to stop Alistar W Headbutt’s engage. Near a turret, don’t give Alistar room to circle behind you and push Xerath under the turret.

Anivia.build: Buy Null-Magic Mantle first to survive early, and choose Mercury’s Treads for boots. Anivia’s main damage is magic, so build magic resistance first.
Anivia.combo: After Anivia Q Flash Frost is down, stun her with Xerath E Shocking Orb, hit the center of Xerath W Eye of Destruction, then fire Xerath Q Arcanopulse. If E misses, don’t use follow-up abilities; save mana. For poke when you aren’t going for a kill, slow her with W first, then fire Q.
Anivia.escape: Look for an angle to attack while Anivia Q Flash Frost and W Crystallize are down. Xerath has no ability to escape on his own, so don’t force your way closer while her crowd control is available.
Anivia.fight: Usually, keep your distance and trade damage by slowing her with Xerath W Eye of Destruction, then using Xerath Q Arcanopulse. If Anivia Q Flash Frost is down and you have an angle to hit with Xerath E Shocking Orb, start a full attack with the stun. If Anivia P Rebirth is still available, go in with allies instead of trying to break the egg alone.
Anivia.laning: Poke with Xerath Q Arcanopulse from behind minions, but don’t push the wave unnecessarily. Look for an opportunity when Anivia steps forward to last-hit, and cancel Q to save mana if the angle is off. If you need to push, secure river vision first, and use basic attacks to trigger Xerath P Mana Surge when it’s safe.
Anivia.phase: Xerath is strongest in the mid game when he has ability power and mana, so pressure Anivia with your range advantage. In the late game, Anivia’s terrain control and Xerath’s positioning matter, so fight from a safe distance.
Anivia.teamfight: Start from the very back and fight in the open lane rather than narrow paths where Anivia W Crystallize can easily block your escape. When your allies lock down an enemy, deal damage with Xerath W Eye of Destruction and R Rite of the Arcane. Since R prevents you from moving, secure a safe position first, and save Xerath E Shocking Orb to stop enemies who get on you.
Anivia.watch: Anivia Q Flash Frost explodes at its recast location and stuns, so stand outside its range from the start instead of trying to sidestep where you expect it to explode. If it hits you or you’re inside a fully grown Anivia R Glacial Storm, Anivia E Frostbite deals greatly increased damage, so leave the storm immediately. Anivia W Crystallize can block your escape in narrow paths, so don’t fight there.

Annie.build: Buy Null-Magic Mantle early to survive, and choose Mercury’s Treads for boots. Annie’s damage is mostly magic, so Xerath should build magic resistance first.
Annie.combo: If Annie P Pyromania’s stun is down and you have an angle to hit with Xerath E Shocking Orb, stun her with Xerath E Shocking Orb, hit the center of Xerath W Eye of Destruction, then follow with Xerath Q Arcanopulse. If Xerath E Shocking Orb is blocked by minions or misses, don’t continue the combo; save mana.
Annie.escape: If Annie just used her stun, pressure her while she builds up the stacks again. Annie has no mobility, so if you can close the gap then, catch her with Xerath E Shocking Orb.
Annie.fight: Annie is open to poke after she uses her stun and steps forward to make up for her short range. Slow her with Xerath W Eye of Destruction, then hit her with Xerath Q Arcanopulse. Save Xerath E Shocking Orb to stop Annie if she comes close.
Annie.laning: Use your range advantage to poke from behind minions, but don’t push the wave unnecessarily. Look for Xerath Q Arcanopulse when Annie steps forward to last-hit; if the angle is off, cancel it instead of firing to save mana.
Annie.teamfight: Start from the backline. If Annie is out of sight or has her stun ready, don’t stand clustered with your allies. After your allies lock down an enemy, deal damage with Xerath W Eye of Destruction and Xerath R Rite of the Arcane, and save Xerath E Shocking Orb to stop anyone who gets on you.
Annie.watch: If white light swirls around Annie, Annie P Pyromania’s stun is ready, so don’t enter ability range. Keep your distance so you aren’t hit by both the area attack from Annie R Summon: Tibbers and the stun, and stay away from the summoned Tibbers too.

Aurora.build: Buy a Null-Magic Mantle first in the early game, and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Aurora’s main damage is magic and Xerath has low magic resistance, so prioritize building magic resistance. If the enemy team has an engaging assassin, buy Zhonya's Hourglass earlier.
Aurora.combo: For a kill opportunity, stun Aurora with Xerath E Shocking Orb, hit the center of Xerath W Eye of Destruction, then finish with Xerath Q Arcanopulse. If Xerath E Shocking Orb misses, don’t continue the combo; save your mana. If Aurora gets close, fire Xerath Q Arcanopulse quickly instead of charging it for long.
Aurora.escape: Don’t go in just because Aurora W Across the Veil is down. Check whether Aurora E The Weirding and Aurora R Between Worlds are down too, and especially look for a chance to stun her with Xerath E Shocking Orb before Aurora R Between Worlds comes back up.
Aurora.fight: When Aurora disappears with W Across the Veil, place Xerath W Eye of Destruction where she’s likely to land and wait for her to reappear. When poking, hit the center of Xerath W Eye of Destruction to slow her, then cast Xerath Q Arcanopulse. If Aurora’s dash is available, save Xerath E Shocking Orb to interrupt her engage.
Aurora.laning: Use Xerath’s range advantage to poke with Xerath Q Arcanopulse from behind minions, and don’t push the lane unnecessarily. Mana is limited early, so look for Aurora only when she steps forward to last-hit, and cancel Xerath Q Arcanopulse if the angle is off. If you need to push, get river vision first.
Aurora.phase: Early Xerath uses a lot of mana and is fragile, so avoid extended trades with Aurora. In the late game, secure a safe position first with Aurora’s engage in mind.
Aurora.teamfight: Xerath starts from the back and deals damage with Xerath W Eye of Destruction and Xerath R Rite of the Arcane when allies lock down the enemy. Save Xerath E Shocking Orb to interrupt Aurora when she engages on you. If Aurora participates in a takedown, Aurora W Across the Veil’s cooldown resets, so don’t leave low-health allies behind when retreating.
Aurora.watch: If you’re hit by Aurora Q Twofold Hex, move out of the straight line between you and Aurora to reduce the return damage. The lower your health, the more damage the return deals, so retreat instead of staying while cursed. Create distance before Aurora R Between Worlds opens to avoid the slow when moving in and out of the area.

Azir.build: In the early game, buy a Null-Magic Mantle first to help you survive, and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Azir’s damage is mainly magic and Xerath has relatively low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first.
Azir.combo: For poke when you don’t have a kill opportunity, place Xerath W Eye of Destruction ahead of Azir’s movement path to hit the center and slow him, then follow with Xerath Q Arcanopulse. After Azir E Shifting Sands is down, if you hit him with Xerath E Shocking Orb, hit the center of W and cast Q while he’s stunned. If E misses, don’t continue the combo; save your mana.
Azir.escape: Right after Azir E Shifting Sands is down is your chance to close the distance or catch him out. If Azir has also used Q Conquering Sands and can’t move his soldiers again, position yourself away from the line of soldiers and look for Xerath E Shocking Orb. Don’t force an engage in a narrow passage while Azir R Emperor’s Divide is available.
Azir.fight: Use Xerath’s range advantage to deal brief bursts of damage and back off, and don’t take extended fights where Azir’s soldiers are placed. Right after you force Azir to use E Shifting Sands, catch him with Xerath E Shocking Orb and unload your damage. After Azir uses Q Conquering Sands to move his soldiers, if they stop in place, position yourself away from their line.
Azir.laning: Poke with Xerath Q Arcanopulse from behind minions, but don’t push the lane unnecessarily. If you need to push, get river vision first, and cast Q when Azir steps forward to last-hit. Save mana by canceling Q if the angle is off, and use Xerath P Mana Surge with basic attacks when it’s safe.
Azir.phase: Azir gets stronger as the game goes on, and Xerath is at risk in the late game if he positions poorly, so fight from a safe distance.
Azir.teamfight: Xerath starts from the back and deals damage with Xerath W Eye of Destruction and R Rite of the Arcane after allies lock down the enemy. Approach from multiple directions in open areas so several allies aren’t knocked back together by Azir R Emperor’s Divide. Save Xerath E Shocking Orb to interrupt anyone who dashes onto you, and secure a safe position before activating R.
Azir.watch: Don’t stand for long on the line of soldiers summoned by Azir W Arise!, and check their new positions and dodge after Azir moves them with Q Conquering Sands. Azir E Shifting Sands is a dash with a shield, so save Xerath E Shocking Orb to interrupt his engage. In narrow passages, Azir R Emperor’s Divide can knock back multiple players and leave a wall of soldiers, so don’t enter clustered together.

Bard.build: Buy a Null-Magic Mantle first in the early game. Bard’s main damage is magic, so build magic resistance, and choose Mercury's Treads for boots to prepare for stuns.
Bard.combo: After Bard E Magical Journey is down, stun him with Xerath E Shocking Orb, hit the center of Xerath W Eye of Destruction while he’s stunned, then cast Xerath Q Arcanopulse. If Xerath E Shocking Orb misses, don’t continue the combo; save your mana.
Bard.escape: The moment after you force Bard to use E Magical Journey is your window to close the distance. If Bard Q Cosmic Binding is also down, enter from an angle where you can hit Xerath E Shocking Orb.
Bard.fight: For trades when you don’t have a kill opportunity, hit Bard with the center of Xerath W Eye of Destruction to slow him, then follow with Xerath Q Arcanopulse. Once Bard E Magical Journey is down, you have a chance to close the distance, but fight from an angle where you can hit Xerath E Shocking Orb.
Bard.laning: Poke with Xerath Q Arcanopulse from behind minions, but don’t push the lane unnecessarily. If the angle for Xerath Q Arcanopulse is off, cancel it to save mana, and use basic attacks to trigger Xerath P Mana Surge when it’s safe. If you see Bard W Caretaker’s Shrine in the lane, step on it to remove it, and alert your team on the minimap if Bard disappears from vision.
Bard.phase: In the late game, poor positioning can get you caught immediately, so keep a safe distance.
Bard.teamfight: Start from the back and deal damage with Xerath W Eye of Destruction and Xerath R Rite of the Arcane when your allies lock down the enemy. Watch for engages through Bard E Magical Journey, and save Xerath E Shocking Orb to interrupt enemies who get on top of you.
Bard.watch: Bard Q Cosmic Binding stuns if it hits a wall or a second target, so don’t stand with a wall behind you or in a straight line with an ally or minion. Bard can flank with E Magical Journey, so watch for his engage angle and save Xerath E Shocking Orb. Don’t fire Xerath R Rite of the Arcane at targets made immune to damage by Bard R Tempered Fate.

Blitzcrank.build: Buy a Null-Magic Mantle first in the early game, and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Blitzcrank Q Rocket Grab and Blitzcrank R Static Field deal magic damage, so build magic resistance first.
Blitzcrank.combo: The reliable combo is to stun with Xerath E Shocking Orb, hit the center of Xerath W Eye of Destruction, then cast Xerath Q Arcanopulse. If Xerath E Shocking Orb is blocked by minions or misses, don’t continue the combo; save your mana. For light poke, use Xerath W Eye of Destruction followed by Xerath Q Arcanopulse.
Blitzcrank.escape: Right after Blitzcrank Q Rocket Grab misses is your chance to step forward and poke with Xerath. Blitzcrank has no ability to create distance on his own, so if you get an opening, stun him with Xerath E Shocking Orb and continue attacking. Don’t approach while Blitzcrank Q Rocket Grab is available.
Blitzcrank.fight: Trade by stepping forward right after Blitzcrank Q Rocket Grab misses or when mana is insufficient. If you don’t have a kill opportunity, slow him with Xerath W Eye of Destruction, then hit Xerath Q Arcanopulse. Keep your distance while his hook is available and save Xerath E Shocking Orb for self-defense.
Blitzcrank.laning: Don’t stand alongside minions; poke with Xerath Q Arcanopulse from behind them. You don’t need to push the lane, and if you do, get river vision first. Push the lane or trade after Blitzcrank Q Rocket Grab misses, and check Blitzcrank’s mana bar the rest of the time.
Blitzcrank.phase: In the late game, one bad position can get you caught, so prioritize a safe position.
Blitzcrank.teamfight: Xerath starts from the back and deals damage with Xerath W Eye of Destruction and Xerath R Rite of the Arcane after allies lock down the enemy. Save Xerath E Shocking Orb to interrupt enemies who get on top of you. Xerath R Rite of the Arcane roots you in place, so secure a safe position before using it.
Blitzcrank.watch: If Blitzcrank Q Rocket Grab pulls you in, it’s easy to get hit by Blitzcrank E Power Fist and Blitzcrank R Static Field as well. Always keep minions in front of you, and stay far from bushes if you don’t have vision in them. When Blitzcrank gets close, save Xerath E Shocking Orb for defense.

Braum.build: Buy a Null-Magic Mantle first in the early game, and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Braum’s main damage is magic and Xerath has low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first; tenacity against stuns and knock-ups is also important for Xerath, who has no mobility spells.
Braum.combo: If Braum’s E Unbreakable shield has been lowered and minions don’t block Xerath E Shocking Orb from your angle, stun him with Xerath E Shocking Orb, hit the center of Xerath W Eye of Destruction, then finish with Xerath Q Arcanopulse. If you don’t hit Xerath E Shocking Orb, don’t continue the reliable combo; save your mana.
Braum.escape: The moment after you force Braum to use W Stand Behind Me is your chance to close the distance and catch him with Xerath E Shocking Orb. If Braum E Unbreakable is up, position your angle so the orb isn’t blocked, either after the shield comes down or from outside the direction Braum is facing.
Braum.fight: For poke when you don’t have a kill opportunity, place Xerath W Eye of Destruction ahead of Braum’s movement path to hit the center and slow him, then follow with Xerath Q Arcanopulse. Keep your distance while Braum W Stand Behind Me is available, and look for a stun with Xerath E Shocking Orb right after he uses it, from an angle where his shield is down.
Braum.laning: Dodge Braum Q Winter’s Bite from behind minions while poking with Xerath Q Arcanopulse, and don’t push the lane unnecessarily. Avoid positions where there’s a gap between minions and you’re facing Braum in a straight line. Mana is limited early, so poke only when you have an angle to hit, and cancel Xerath Q Arcanopulse instead of casting if the angle is off.
Braum.phase: Positioning is especially important in the late game, so watch for Braum’s engage and fight from a safe distance.
Braum.teamfight: Start from the back and don’t stand in the line of Braum R Glacial Fissure. Deal damage with Xerath W Eye of Destruction and Xerath R Rite of the Arcane after allies lock down the enemy, but activate R only after securing a safe position. Find an angle that avoids the front of Braum E Unbreakable, and save Xerath E Shocking Orb to interrupt enemies who get on top of you.
Braum.watch: If Braum Q Winter’s Bite or a basic attack applies a Braum P Concussive Blows stack, move out of range before more stun stacks build up. When you see Braum R Glacial Fissure’s cast animation, dodge out of its line, and don’t step on the slow zone it leaves behind. Projectiles are blocked in the direction Braum E Unbreakable is facing, so cast Xerath E Shocking Orb after his shield comes down.

Corki.build: Buy Cloth Armor first in the early game, and choose Plated Steelcaps for boots. Corki’s main damage is physical, so build armor first. You also need health, since resistance cannot block the true damage from Corki P Hextech Munitions.
Corki.combo: After Corki W Valkyrie is down, stun him with Xerath E Shocking Orb, hit the center of Xerath W Eye of Destruction while he is stunned, then fire Xerath Q Arcanopulse. If Xerath E Shocking Orb misses, don’t continue the combo; save your mana.
Corki.escape: The moment after Corki uses W Valkyrie is your window to engage. Land Xerath E Shocking Orb while his mobility is down to stop him from escaping.
Corki.fight: For poke that is not meant to secure a kill, slow Corki first with Xerath W Eye of Destruction, then hit him with Xerath Q Arcanopulse. Don’t force an engage while Corki W Valkyrie is available; look for a chance to land Xerath E Shocking Orb right after he uses it. Keep moving to the side to trade around the front of Corki E Gatling Gun.
Corki.laning: Pressure Corki when he steps forward to last-hit, but save Xerath E Shocking Orb for after Corki W Valkyrie. If you need to push the lane, secure river vision first.
Corki.phase: Corki gets stronger as he builds items, so in the late game, reposition to avoid consecutive missile hits and stay somewhere safe.
Corki.teamfight: Start from the far back and deal damage with Xerath W Eye of Destruction and Xerath R Rite of the Arcane after your team locks down an enemy. Save Xerath E Shocking Orb to interrupt anyone who gets on top of you. Xerath R Rite of the Arcane roots you in place, so find a safe position before using it.
Corki.watch: Corki R Missile Barrage also damages enemies near the first target it hits, so move out of range instead of hiding behind minions. Reposition to avoid being hit repeatedly, especially by the third missile. Corki E Gatling Gun reduces your armor and magic resistance if it hits you, so move to the side instead of standing your ground in front of it.

Ekko.build: Ekko mainly deals magic damage, and Xerath has relatively low magic resistance, so buy Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury’s Treads. Since Ekko can engage on and catch Xerath, build Zhonya’s Hourglass earlier in case he engages while Xerath E Shocking Orb is down or while you’re using Xerath R Rite of the Arcane.
Ekko.combo: When you have a clear chance to kill Ekko, stun him with Xerath E Shocking Orb, hit the center of Xerath W Eye of Destruction, then follow with Xerath Q Arcanopulse. If Xerath E Shocking Orb misses, stop the follow-up and save your mana. Use Xerath R Rite of the Arcane from a safe position, after first locking Ekko down with Xerath E Shocking Orb or Xerath W Eye of Destruction.
Ekko.escape: Right after Ekko closes in with E Phase Dive, his mobility is down, giving you a chance to stun him with Xerath E Shocking Orb. When going in to attack, don’t treat Ekko E Phase Dive being down as enough; look for a window when Ekko W Parallel Convergence and Ekko R Chronobreak are down too.
Ekko.fight: For poke, hit the center of Xerath W Eye of Destruction to slow Ekko, then fire Xerath Q Arcanopulse. If Ekko closes in with E Phase Dive, interrupt him with Xerath E Shocking Orb, and look for a chance to attack while Ekko R Chronobreak is down. It’s a good time to fight seriously if both Ekko W Parallel Convergence and Ekko R Chronobreak are down.
Ekko.laning: Use your range advantage to poke with Xerath Q Arcanopulse from behind minions, but don’t push the lane unless you need to. Look for Ekko when he steps forward to last-hit, and cancel Xerath Q Arcanopulse if your aim is off to save mana. If you need to push, secure river vision first, and use basic attacks to trigger Xerath P Mana Surge only when it’s safe.
Ekko.phase: In the late game, you’re easy to catch with an engage, so find a safe position first.
Ekko.teamfight: Start from the far back and deal damage with Xerath W Eye of Destruction and Xerath R Rite of the Arcane when your team locks down an enemy. If Ekko closes in with E Phase Dive, interrupt him with Xerath E Shocking Orb, and leave any area where you see the signal for Ekko W Parallel Convergence. During sieges or standoffs around objectives, pressure enemies with Xerath Q Arcanopulse from beyond a wall or behind a turret.
Ekko.watch: If you see the signal for Ekko W Parallel Convergence, stay out of its area to avoid the stun and shield. Note the direction Ekko Q Timewinder travels and dodge its return path too. If you see Ekko’s afterimage behind him, Ekko R Chronobreak is ready, so don’t chase recklessly even when health is low.

Fizz.build: Fizz mainly deals magic damage, and Xerath has relatively low magic resistance, so buy Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury’s Treads for boots. Build Zhonya’s Hourglass earlier to prepare for Fizz’s engage.
Fizz.combo: When Fizz E Playful / Trickster is down, stun him with Xerath E Shocking Orb, hit the center of Xerath W Eye of Destruction, then finish with Xerath Q Arcanopulse. If Xerath E Shocking Orb misses, don’t continue the combo; save your mana. For poke that is not meant to secure a kill, slow him with Xerath W Eye of Destruction, then fire Xerath Q Arcanopulse.
Fizz.escape: While Fizz E Playful / Trickster is down, land Xerath E Shocking Orb and look for a chance to attack. Fizz Q Urchin Strike may still be available, so don’t approach recklessly just because Fizz E Playful / Trickster is down.
Fizz.fight: Counterattack by landing Xerath E Shocking Orb right after Fizz E Playful / Trickster is down. When Fizz comes in with Q Urchin Strike, he has to walk into range, so save Xerath E Shocking Orb to interrupt his dash. It’s also a chance to trade when he misses a last hit with the empowered basic attack from Fizz W Seastone Trident.
Fizz.laning: Poke with Xerath Q Arcanopulse from behind minions, but don’t push the lane unless you need to. Look for Fizz when he steps forward to last-hit, and cancel Xerath Q Arcanopulse if your aim is off to save mana. If you need to push, secure river vision first.
Fizz.phase: In the late game, a poor position can let Fizz engage and kill you immediately, so keep a safe distance.
Fizz.teamfight: Stay with your allies and start from the far back. Save Xerath E Shocking Orb to interrupt Fizz when he gets on you. When Fizz E Playful / Trickster is down, focus fire with your team. After your team locks down an enemy, deal damage with Xerath W Eye of Destruction and Xerath R Rite of the Arcane, but use Xerath R Rite of the Arcane only after finding a safe position.
Fizz.watch: Fizz Q Urchin Strike and Fizz E Playful / Trickster are ways for him to reach Xerath, so don’t relax just because one of them is down. If Fizz R Chum the Waters attaches to you, move away from your allies before the shark erupts, and aim Xerath E Shocking Orb at Fizz’s approach path.

Galio.build: Build Null-Magic Mantle first to hold on in the early game, then choose Mercury’s Treads for boots. Galio mainly deals magic damage, and Xerath has relatively low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first.
Galio.combo: After dodging Galio E Justice Punch and Galio W Shield of Durand, stun him with Xerath E Shocking Orb. While he’s stunned, hit the center of Xerath W Eye of Destruction, then fire Xerath Q Arcanopulse. If Xerath E Shocking Orb misses, don’t continue the combo; save your mana. For poke that is not meant to secure a kill, slow him first with Xerath W Eye of Destruction, then fire Xerath Q Arcanopulse.
Galio.escape: Don’t move forward just because Galio E Justice Punch is down. Keep your distance and attack with Xerath E Shocking Orb during a window when Galio R Hero’s Entrance is not yet back and Galio W Shield of Durand is also down.
Galio.fight: Keep your distance when Galio approaches for a melee attack. Slow him with Xerath W Eye of Destruction, then poke with Xerath Q Arcanopulse. While Galio W Shield of Durand is charging, hold your damage and move out of taunt range. If he tries to close in with Galio E Justice Punch, interrupt the engage with Xerath E Shocking Orb.
Galio.laning: Use your range advantage to poke with Xerath Q Arcanopulse from behind minions, but conserve mana early and fire only when you can hit. Don’t push the lane unless you need to; if you do, secure river vision first. If Galio spends abilities and mana clearing the wave, pushing the lane can limit his chance to intervene in other lanes with Galio R Hero’s Entrance.
Galio.phase: Early on, Xerath is fragile and spends a lot of mana, so limit your poke, but use your range to pressure melee Galio. In the late game, a poor position can leave you caught by Galio’s engage and crowd control, so keep a safe distance.
Galio.teamfight: Start from the far back, and immediately walk out of the area if you see the landing marker for Galio R Hero’s Entrance. After your team locks down an enemy, deal damage with Xerath W Eye of Destruction and Xerath R Rite of the Arcane, but cast the immobile Xerath R Rite of the Arcane from a safe position. Save Xerath E Shocking Orb to interrupt Galio if he engages on you.
Galio.watch: When you see Galio W Shield of Durand charging, don’t spend your damage on Galio while his damage taken is reduced; walk out of taunt range. Dodge when Galio E Justice Punch shows its windup of stepping back, and save Xerath E Shocking Orb to interrupt his dash. Avoid the point where both gusts from Galio Q Winds of War overlap, and immediately leave the area when you see the landing marker for Galio R Hero’s Entrance.

Hwei.build: Buy Null-Magic Mantle first in the early game, and choose Mercury’s Treads for boots. Hwei mainly deals magic damage, and Xerath has relatively low magic resistance, so prioritize magic resistance. Hwei Q Subject: Disaster deals damage based on your maximum health, so don’t rely on building only health.
Hwei.combo: For a guaranteed combo, stun him with Xerath E Shocking Orb from an angle that minions won’t block, hit the center of Xerath W Eye of Destruction, then finish with Xerath Q Arcanopulse. If Xerath E Shocking Orb misses, don’t force the follow-up spells; save your mana. For light poke, land the slow from Xerath W Eye of Destruction first, then follow with Xerath Q Arcanopulse.
Hwei.escape: Hwei has no mobility ability, so the moment after he uses E Subject: Torment for poke or wave clear is your window to attack. Stun him then with Xerath E Shocking Orb from an angle that minions won’t block, and follow up with more abilities. If Hwei E Subject: Torment is available, keep your distance and watch for its root or forced movement.
Hwei.fight: For trades that aren’t meant to secure a kill, place Xerath W Eye of Destruction ahead of Hwei’s movement to hit the center slow, then fire Xerath Q Arcanopulse. Hwei has fewer ways to retaliate right after using E Subject: Torment for poke or wave clear, so look for a chance to attack. If you’re hit by the first ability, don’t insist on trading; move to dodge the follow-up abilities.
Hwei.laning: Poke with Xerath Q Arcanopulse from behind minions, but don’t push the lane unless you need to. Look for Hwei when he steps forward to last-hit, and cancel Xerath Q Arcanopulse if your aim is off to save mana. If you need to push, secure river vision first, and use a basic attack on a champion to trigger Xerath P Mana Surge when it’s safe.
Hwei.phase: In the late game, a poor position can get you engaged on and killed, so fight from the back.
Hwei.teamfight: Start from the far back, and deal damage with Xerath W Eye of Destruction and Xerath R Rite of the Arcane after your team locks down Hwei or another enemy. Save Xerath E Shocking Orb to interrupt anyone who gets on top of you. You cannot move during Xerath R Rite of the Arcane, so find a safe position before using it; if Hwei disappears from vision, you can end the channel without firing a shot.
Hwei.watch: If you’re caught by Hwei E Subject: Torment’s root or pull, you’re likely to take follow-up damage, so keep your distance while this ability is available. Hwei Q Subject: Disaster deals damage based on your maximum health, and if you’re hit by other abilities in succession too, Hwei P Signature of the Visionary’s damage detonates; reposition as soon as you’re hit by the first ability. Don’t cross dangerous paths Hwei has laid down; take a wide route around them.

Irelia.build: Early on, buy Cloth Armor first, then choose Plated Steelcaps for boots. Irelia mainly deals physical damage, and Xerath has relatively low armor, so build armor first.
Irelia.combo: When you have a chance to kill, stun her with Xerath E Shocking Orb, hit the center of Xerath W Eye of Destruction, then fire Xerath Q Arcanopulse. For poke, slow her first with Xerath W Eye of Destruction, then hit her with Xerath Q Arcanopulse. If Irelia is close, don’t charge Xerath Q Arcanopulse for long; fire it quickly.
Irelia.escape: Right after Irelia Q Bladesurge is down, you have a chance to close the distance or catch her. Stun her then with Xerath E Shocking Orb, but if Irelia can still dash, save Xerath E Shocking Orb to interrupt her engage.
Irelia.fight: Normally, when Irelia steps forward to last-hit, slow her with Xerath W Eye of Destruction, then poke with Xerath Q Arcanopulse. Right after Irelia Q Bladesurge is down, look for a chance to fight by landing Xerath E Shocking Orb. If Xerath E Shocking Orb misses, don’t continue the combo; save your mana.
Irelia.laning: Use your range advantage to poke from behind minions, but position so there are no low-health minions between you and Irelia. Don’t push the lane unless you need to; if you do, secure river vision first. To conserve mana, fire Xerath Q Arcanopulse only when you have a clear angle, and cancel it if your aim is off.
Irelia.phase: In the late game, poor positioning can let an enemy engage on you and take you down immediately, so keep your distance.
Irelia.teamfight: Start from the far back, and prioritize Irelia, who can take over a team fight. When your team locks her down, deal damage with Xerath W Eye of Destruction and Xerath R Rite of the Arcane. Save Xerath E Shocking Orb to interrupt Irelia if she gets on you. Xerath R Rite of the Arcane roots you in place, so find a safe position before using it.
Irelia.watch: Irelia Q Bladesurge can chain dashes through low-health minions to close in, so step back when minions are about to die. Watch out for Irelia E Flawless Duet’s stun, and if you’re trapped inside Irelia R Vanguard’s Edge’s perimeter, wait until the blades disappear.

Janna.build: Build a Null-Magic Mantle early to survive, and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Since Janna deals mostly magic damage and Xerath tends to have low magic resistance, prioritize magic resistance if you need it.
Janna.combo: Your reliable combo is to stun with Xerath E Shocking Orb, hit the center of Xerath W Eye of Destruction, then fire Xerath Q Arcanopulse. Against a target protected by Janna E Eye Of The Storm, use the combo after the shield is gone or target someone else. If Xerath E Shocking Orb misses, don't continue the combo; save your mana.
Janna.escape: Your opening comes when Janna Q Howling Gale is down and the shield from Janna E Eye Of The Storm is gone. If Janna is isolated, find an angle where minions won't block Xerath E Shocking Orb and stun her. Janna R Monsoon can push enemies out of a fight, so don't waste Xerath E Shocking Orb beforehand.
Janna.fight: For poke that isn't a kill attempt, slow Janna by hitting the center of Xerath W Eye of Destruction, then follow up with Xerath Q Arcanopulse. Don't spend all your damage on a target protected by Janna E Eye Of The Storm; look for an opportunity after the shield is gone. If Janna is isolated and Janna Q Howling Gale is down, look for an angle where minions won't block Xerath E Shocking Orb and try to stun her.
Janna.laning: Poke with Xerath Q Arcanopulse from behind minions, but don't push the wave unnecessarily. Harass the ally Janna is protecting to make her use Janna E Eye Of The Storm, then look to take control if Janna Q Howling Gale and Janna W Zephyr are wasted. Conserve mana early and only fire when you have a good angle; use basic attacks to trigger Xerath P Mana Surge when it's safe.
Janna.phase: In the late game, poor positioning can put you in danger, so keep a safe distance.
Janna.teamfight: Start from the far back and deal damage with Xerath W Eye of Destruction and Xerath R Rite of the Arcane after your allies lock down the enemy. If you need to interrupt Janna R Monsoon, save Xerath E Shocking Orb for that moment; use it defensively if an enemy gets on you. Xerath R Rite of the Arcane roots you in place, so find a safe position before casting it.
Janna.watch: Janna Q Howling Gale makes a sound as it charges, so if you hear it from a brush or outside your vision, move out of its path. Keep Janna W Zephyr's slow and movement speed increase in mind and create distance before charging Xerath Q Arcanopulse for a long time. Janna R Monsoon knocks enemies back and heals, so watch for when she uses it during a fight.

Karma.build: Early on, buy a Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Karma's main damage is magic, so Xerath should prioritize magic resistance. Keep enough distance to break Karma W Focused Resolve's tether and get out of Karma Q Inner Flame's range.
Karma.combo: When Karma W Focused Resolve is down and you have an angle where minions won't block it, stun her with Xerath E Shocking Orb. If Xerath E Shocking Orb misses, stop the combo and save your mana.
Karma.escape: When Karma W Focused Resolve is down, you have a chance to close the distance. Once Karma E Inspire's movement speed increase and shield have also expired, landing Xerath E Shocking Orb can keep Karma locked down.
Karma.fight: For trades that aren't kill attempts, place Xerath W Eye of Destruction ahead of Karma's direction of movement to hit the center, then fire Xerath Q Arcanopulse. Keep your distance while Karma W Focused Resolve is available; once it is down, look for Xerath E Shocking Orb from an angle where minions won't block it. If Karma R Mantra-enhanced Karma E Inspire's shield is active, fight after its duration ends.
Karma.laning: Conserve mana early by poking with Xerath Q Arcanopulse from behind minions, and don't push the wave unnecessarily. Look for moments when Karma steps forward to last-hit or backs away, and cancel Xerath Q Arcanopulse instead of firing if your angle is off. If you need to push the wave, secure river vision first; use basic attacks to trigger Xerath P Mana Surge when it's safe.
Karma.phase: In the late game, poor positioning makes you easy to catch, so start from a safe distance.
Karma.teamfight: Start from the far back, then deal damage with Xerath W Eye of Destruction and Xerath R Rite of the Arcane as your allies engage after Karma W Focused Resolve is down. If Karma R Mantra-enhanced Karma E Inspire's shield is on nearby allies, hold your burst until it ends. Save Xerath E Shocking Orb to stop enemies who get on you.
Karma.watch: When you are hit by Karma Q Inner Flame, Karma P Gathering Fire reduces Karma R Mantra's cooldown. Walk out of the ground effect left by Karma Q Inner Flame empowered by Karma R Mantra as soon as you are hit. If you are tethered by Karma W Focused Resolve, create distance to break it before you are rooted.

Kassadin.build: Early on, buy a Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Kassadin deals mostly magic damage, so build magic resistance and buy Zhonya's Hourglass earlier to prepare for his engage.
Kassadin.combo: For a kill attempt, stun with Xerath E Shocking Orb, hit the center of W Eye of Destruction, then follow with Q Arcanopulse. If E misses, don't continue the combo; save your mana. For light poke, wait until Kassadin Q Null Sphere is down, then slow him with W and fire Q.
Kassadin.escape: You have a chance to punish while Kassadin R Riftwalk is down. If Kassadin E Force Pulse's slow is also down, stun him with Xerath E Shocking Orb, then follow with W Eye of Destruction and Q Arcanopulse. If Kassadin has used R repeatedly, check his mana bar to see whether he still has a mobility option available.
Kassadin.fight: After the shield from Kassadin Q Null Sphere is down, slow him with Xerath W Eye of Destruction and hit him with Q Arcanopulse. If Kassadin can engage with Kassadin R Riftwalk, don't use Xerath E Shocking Orb first.
Kassadin.laning: Avoid unnecessary casts near Kassadin, since using abilities reduces Kassadin E Force Pulse's cooldown.
Kassadin.phase: The mid game is when Xerath grows stronger with ability power and mana, but you still need to position with Kassadin R Riftwalk in mind. In the late game, Kassadin can reach the backline, so don't stand alone within his R range.
Kassadin.teamfight: Start from the far back and deal damage with Xerath W Eye of Destruction and R Rite of the Arcane after your allies lock down Kassadin. Save Xerath E Shocking Orb to stop Kassadin's engage. You can't move while channeling R, so find a safe position before casting it.
Kassadin.watch: Kassadin Q Null Sphere absorbs magic damage with its shield and interrupts channels, so charge Xerath Q Arcanopulse or begin Xerath R Rite of the Arcane after it is down.

Leblanc.build: Early on, buy a Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. LeBlanc deals mostly magic damage, so build magic resistance. Buy Zhonya's Hourglass earlier to prepare for her engage, including when Xerath E Shocking Orb is unavailable or you get caught during Xerath R Rite of the Arcane.
Leblanc.combo: When you have a clear opening, stun with Xerath E Shocking Orb, hit the center of Xerath W Eye of Destruction, then follow with Xerath Q Arcanopulse. If Xerath E Shocking Orb misses, don't continue the combo; save your mana. For poke only, hit with Xerath W Eye of Destruction first, then fire Xerath Q Arcanopulse.
Leblanc.escape: Right after you force LeBlanc to use W Distortion, you have a chance to close the distance or catch her out. Confirm that its return has expired or already been used, then stun her with Xerath E Shocking Orb and attack. While Xerath E Shocking Orb is unavailable, you have few ways to stop LeBlanc's engage, so keep your distance.
Leblanc.fight: For trades that aren't kill attempts, slow LeBlanc with Xerath W Eye of Destruction, then hit her with Xerath Q Arcanopulse. Keep Xerath E Shocking Orb for defense while LeBlanc can engage with W Distortion. Punish after LeBlanc W Distortion's return expires or has already been used.
Leblanc.laning: Use your range advantage to poke with Xerath Q Arcanopulse from behind minions, and don't push the wave unnecessarily. Cancel Xerath Q Arcanopulse to save mana if your angle is off, and don't step forward while LeBlanc Q Sigil of Malice's mark is on you. If LeBlanc disappears from vision, alert your team immediately; if you need to push, secure river vision first.
Leblanc.phase: In the late game, one positioning mistake can let an enemy engage, so prioritize keeping a safe distance.
Leblanc.teamfight: Start from the far back and save Xerath E Shocking Orb to stop LeBlanc if she gets on you. Deal damage with Xerath W Eye of Destruction and Xerath R Rite of the Arcane after your allies lock down the enemy. Xerath R Rite of the Arcane roots you in place, so find a safe position before casting it.
Leblanc.watch: If LeBlanc Q Sigil of Malice's mark is still on you, back away so you don't get hit by her next ability. Save Xerath E Shocking Orb for when LeBlanc uses W Distortion to engage, and if LeBlanc E Ethereal Chains hits you, get out of chain range before you are rooted. If LeBlanc creates a clone after losing health, don't waste abilities; identify which one is actually attacking.

Leona.build: Early on, buy a Null-Magic Mantle first to build magic resistance. Choose Mercury's Treads for boots.
Leona.combo: After Leona E Zenith Blade is down, stun her with Xerath E Shocking Orb, then hit the center of Xerath W Eye of Destruction and fire Xerath Q Arcanopulse. If Xerath E Shocking Orb misses, don't continue the combo; save your mana.
Leona.escape: The moment Leona E Zenith Blade misses or goes down is your chance to close the distance. If Leona Q Shield of Daybreak and the crowd control from Leona R Solar Flare are also down, try to stun her with Xerath E Shocking Orb.
Leona.fight: Keep your distance until Leona E Zenith Blade is down. To poke, slow her with Xerath W Eye of Destruction, then fire Xerath Q Arcanopulse. If Leona engages, use Xerath E Shocking Orb to defend yourself.
Leona.laning: Use your range to poke from behind minions, and don't push the wave unnecessarily. Xerath E Shocking Orb is blocked by minions, so find an angle where Leona and the minions aren't lined up. Conserve mana and only fire Xerath Q Arcanopulse when you have a good angle; if you need to push, secure river vision first.
Leona.phase: Early on, Xerath is fragile and uses a lot of mana, so be careful of Leona's engage and poke sparingly. In the late game, a positioning mistake can let her engage and take you down, so keep your distance more strictly.
Leona.teamfight: Start from the far back and deal damage with Xerath W Eye of Destruction and Xerath R Rite of the Arcane after your allies lock down the enemy. Save Xerath E Shocking Orb to stop enemies who get on you, and cast Xerath R Rite of the Arcane from a safe position. If Leona P Sunlight marks you, the enemy can follow up with more damage, so back away immediately.
Leona.watch: If Leona E Zenith Blade hits you, she can close in and chain crowd control, so don't give her the range to reach you. When Leona R Solar Flare's marker appears, move sideways to avoid the center stun. When Leona activates W Eclipse, retreat out of its range before it explodes.

Lissandra.build: Early on, buy a Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Lissandra deals mostly magic damage and Xerath tends to have low magic resistance, so prioritize magic resistance. Also get tenacity to prepare for getting caught by a root or stun and hit by follow-up damage.
Lissandra.combo: Stun Lissandra with Xerath E Shocking Orb when Lissandra E Glacial Path is down or when you can interrupt her movement. If Xerath E Shocking Orb misses, don't continue the combo; save your mana.
Lissandra.escape: The moment after Lissandra E Glacial Path has been used is your chance to close the distance. If Lissandra W Ring of Frost is also used on the wave or misses, start a trade and stun her with Xerath E Shocking Orb so she can't escape. If Lissandra E Glacial Path is still traveling, interrupt her movement with Xerath E Shocking Orb before she recasts.
Lissandra.fight: For poke that isn't a kill attempt, slow Lissandra by hitting the center of Xerath W Eye of Destruction, then fire Xerath Q Arcanopulse. You have a trading window just after Lissandra W Ring of Frost is used on the wave or misses. Save Xerath E Shocking Orb to interrupt her engage while Lissandra E Glacial Path is available.
Lissandra.laning: Poke from behind minions with Xerath Q Arcanopulse's range, but offset your position from allied minions to avoid Lissandra Q Ice Shard's piercing path. Don't push the wave unnecessarily; if you need to push, secure river vision first. Mana is limited early, so poke only when you have a good angle and use basic attacks to trigger Xerath P Mana Surge when it's safe.
Lissandra.phase: Early on, Xerath uses a lot of mana and is fragile, so conserve your poke and keep your distance. In the late game, find a safe position first to avoid getting caught by an engage.
Lissandra.teamfight: Start from the far back and deal damage with Xerath W Eye of Destruction and Xerath R Rite of the Arcane after your allies lock down the enemy. Save Xerath E Shocking Orb to stop enemies who get on you, and cast Xerath R Rite of the Arcane, which roots you in place, from a safe position. If Lissandra can cast Lissandra R Frozen Tomb on herself, don't dump all your finishing damage at once; deal damage after her damage immunity ends as well.
Lissandra.watch: Lissandra Q Ice Shard pierces after hitting a minion, so don't stand in a line with allied minions. When Lissandra E Glacial Path is traveling toward you, look for an angle to interrupt it with Xerath E Shocking Orb before she recasts to move. Keep your distance because Lissandra W Ring of Frost's root and Lissandra R Frozen Tomb's stun make it easy to take follow-up damage.

Lux.build: Early on, buy a Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Lux deals mostly magic damage and Xerath tends to have low magic resistance, so prioritize magic resistance.
Lux.combo: After Lux Q Light Binding misses, if you see a kill opportunity, stun her with Xerath E Shocking Orb, then hit the center of Xerath W Eye of Destruction and fire Xerath Q Arcanopulse. If E is blocked by a minion or misses, don't continue the combo; save your mana.
Lux.escape: Bait Lux Q Light Binding, dodge it, then close the distance. Lux has no mobility ability, so if you get in range, stun her with Xerath E Shocking Orb to create an opportunity to attack.
Lux.fight: After dodging Lux Q Light Binding, you have a good window to deal damage. For poke that isn't a kill attempt, slow her first with Xerath W Eye of Destruction, then fire Xerath Q Arcanopulse. When you have a chance to close the distance, hit Lux, who has no mobility ability, with Xerath E Shocking Orb to stun her.
Lux.laning: Poke with Xerath Q Arcanopulse from behind minions, but don't stand in a line with your allies because Lux Q Light Binding roots the first two enemies it hits. Look for Q when Lux steps forward to last-hit, and cancel the cast to save mana if your angle is off. Don't push the wave unnecessarily; if you need to push, secure river vision first.
Lux.phase: Early on, Xerath is fragile and limited in how often he can poke by his mana, so farm carefully while watching out for Lux Q Light Binding. In the late game, a positioning mistake can make you easy to catch, so keep a safe distance.
Lux.teamfight: Start from the very back and don't group with your allies where Lux E Lucent Singularity can hit you all. Deal damage with Xerath W Eye of Destruction and Xerath R Rite of the Arcane after your allies lock down the enemy, but cast R from a safe position. Save Xerath E Shocking Orb to stop enemies who get on you.
Lux.watch: If Lux Q Light Binding hits you, her follow-up abilities are likely to land too, so don't stand in a line with your allies and dodge Q. Walk out of the area where Lux E Lucent Singularity lands, and dodge sideways when you see the red targeting line from Lux R Final Spark. If Lux hits you with an ability, move out of basic attack range so Lux P Illumination can't be triggered by a basic attack.

Malzahar.build: Early on, buy Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Malzahar's main damage is magic, so build magic resistance first.
Malzahar.combo: Break Malzahar P Void Shift first, then stun him with Xerath E Shocking Orb, hit the center of Xerath W Eye of Destruction, and follow with Xerath Q Arcanopulse. If Xerath E Shocking Orb misses, don't continue the combo; save your mana.
Malzahar.escape: Malzahar has no ability to create distance on his own, so after breaking Malzahar P Void Shift and dodging the silence from Malzahar Q Call of the Void, look for a chance to hit Xerath E Shocking Orb. While Malzahar R Nether Grasp is available, don't enter areas without vision alone.
Malzahar.fight: If Malzahar P Void Shift is active, break it first with Xerath W Eye of Destruction, then look for Xerath E Shocking Orb. For poke that isn't a kill attempt, slow him with Xerath W Eye of Destruction, then hit Xerath Q Arcanopulse. Keep your distance since Malzahar's immobilizing abilities make it easy for him to land follow-up attacks.
Malzahar.laning: Poke with Xerath Q Arcanopulse from behind minions, but don't push the lane unnecessarily. If Malzahar casts Malzahar E Malefic Visions on the wave, don't stand beside it looking for last hits; back away until the minions are cleared. If Malzahar pushes the lane and Malzahar P Void Shift has been broken, look for a chance to take him down with your jungler.
Malzahar.phase: Xerath spends a lot of mana early, so choose your poke carefully, but use pressure to limit the time Malzahar has to scale. Positioning matters late, so stay far back at a safe distance.
Malzahar.teamfight: Start from the very back and deal damage with Xerath W Eye of Destruction and Xerath R Rite of the Arcane when your allies lock down an opponent. If Malzahar W Void Swarm's summoned creatures are already in place, clear them first with an area-of-effect ability. Save Xerath E Shocking Orb to stop enemies who get on top of you, and use Xerath R Rite of the Arcane from a safe position.
Malzahar.watch: If you are standing beside minions affected by Malzahar E Malefic Visions, take a step back, since the damage can spread to you when they die. When you see Malzahar Q Call of the Void, hold your abilities and move from between the two portals to outside the portals. While Malzahar R Nether Grasp is available, don't cross areas without vision alone.

Maokai.build: Early on, buy Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Build magic resistance first to counter Maokai's magic damage; after that, choose resistances based on the enemy damage dealer who will attack while Maokai has you caught.
Maokai.combo: When Maokai W Twisted Advance is down and you have an angle for Xerath E Shocking Orb, stun him, hit the center of Xerath W Eye of Destruction, then follow with Xerath Q Arcanopulse. If Xerath E Shocking Orb misses, save your follow-up abilities. For poke that isn't a kill attempt, slow him with Xerath W Eye of Destruction, then fire Xerath Q Arcanopulse.
Maokai.escape: The moment after you make Maokai use Maokai W Twisted Advance is your window to close the distance. After his dash ends, hit Xerath E Shocking Orb to start a trade. While Maokai R Nature's Grasp is available, make sure you have room to dodge its root.
Maokai.fight: Keep your distance while Maokai W Twisted Advance is available, and step forward to trade right after it has been used.
Maokai.laning: Use your range advantage to poke from behind minions, but don't push the lane unnecessarily. Maokai P Sap Magic comes back faster when he is hit by abilities, so don't spam abilities on him. Use Xerath P Mana Surge with a basic attack when it's safe. If you need to push the lane, secure river vision first.
Maokai.phase: Early on, Xerath is fragile and short on mana, so focus on farming and managing your distance. Late in the game, one positioning mistake can let the enemy engage, so stay safely behind your team.
Maokai.teamfight: Start from the very back and deal damage with Xerath W Eye of Destruction and Xerath R Rite of the Arcane after your allies lock down an opponent. Save Xerath E Shocking Orb to stop enemies who get on top of you. Fight in open terrain rather than narrow passages so you can sidestep Maokai R Nature's Grasp.
Maokai.watch: Maokai W Twisted Advance dashes in and roots you, so don't approach the brush while it's available. Don't enter brush where Maokai E Sapling Toss has planted a sapling, and dodge Maokai R Nature's Grasp at a right angle to its path when it comes from far away.

Mel.build: Buy Null-Magic Mantle first to withstand Mel's magic damage early. Choose Mercury's Treads and prioritize magic resistance.
Mel.combo: When Mel W Rebuttal is down and you have an angle for Xerath E Shocking Orb, stun her with E, hit the center of Xerath W Eye of Destruction, then follow with Xerath Q Arcanopulse. If E misses, stop the combo and save your mana.
Mel.escape: After Mel W Rebuttal and Mel E Solar Snare are down, you have a chance to step forward and pressure her. Mel has no mobility, so hitting Xerath E Shocking Orb from a safe distance makes it easy to follow up with more attacks.
Mel.fight: Poke while Mel W Rebuttal is down, using your range advantage. If you aren't going for a kill, hit the center of Xerath W Eye of Destruction to slow her, then fire Xerath Q Arcanopulse. Use Xerath E Shocking Orb when you have an angle to stun Mel, but save it if you need to stop an enemy approaching you.
Mel.laning: Conserve mana early and look for moments when Mel steps forward to farm, poking with Xerath Q Arcanopulse from behind minions. Pressure her to slow her growth, but don't push the lane recklessly. If you need to push, secure river vision first so the immobile Xerath doesn't get caught by a gank.
Mel.phase: Pressure Mel safely from the start, before she gets stronger. Xerath comes online in the mid game as he builds ability power and mana. Late in the game, Mel's scaling adds up and Xerath is vulnerable to positioning mistakes, so be extra careful to maintain your distance.
Mel.teamfight: Start from the very back and deal damage with Xerath W Eye of Destruction and Xerath R Rite of the Arcane when your allies lock down an opponent. If Mel W Rebuttal is still available, don't use Xerath E Shocking Orb carelessly; look for a chance to stop enemies who get on top of you. Xerath R Rite of the Arcane roots you in place, so secure a safe position before using it.
Mel.watch: Mel W Rebuttal can block Xerath E Shocking Orb if you throw it while Rebuttal is active, so test her reaction with a basic attack first and use E after W is down. Mel E Solar Snare roots you if it hits in the center, making it easy for her to follow with Mel Q Radiant Volley, so sidestep it. If you've been hit by Mel's attacks several times, watch out for the execute from Mel P Searing Brilliance even if you still have health. After a fight, stay somewhere safe until the stacks disappear.

Milio.build: Buy Null-Magic Mantle first to survive early, then choose Mercury's Treads. Milio deals magic damage, so build magic resistance. If Milio W Cozy Campfire and Milio R Breath of Life make fights longer, get healing reduction after your resistance.
Milio.combo: The reliable combo is to stun with Xerath E Shocking Orb, hit the center of Xerath W Eye of Destruction, then finish with Xerath Q Arcanopulse. Look for this opening when Milio Q Ultra Mega Fire Kick is down. If Xerath E Shocking Orb misses, don't use follow-up abilities; save your mana.
Milio.escape: Milio Q Ultra Mega Fire Kick is his only way to disengage, so after it's down, you have a chance to close the distance on him. If you get close, stun him with Xerath E Shocking Orb so he can't get away.
Milio.fight: For poke that isn't a kill attempt, slow the target by hitting the center of Xerath W Eye of Destruction, then land Xerath Q Arcanopulse. If Milio Q Ultra Mega Fire Kick is down, you have a chance to close the distance, but stun Milio with Xerath E Shocking Orb from a safe position before following up with damage.
Milio.laning: Use your range advantage to poke from behind minions, but don't push the lane too hard. Look for Xerath Q Arcanopulse only when Milio steps forward or retreats; if your angle is off, cancel the cast to save mana. If you need to push the lane, secure river vision first.
Milio.phase: Milio's team composition gets stronger over time, so Xerath needs to stay in a particularly safe position late in the game.
Milio.teamfight: Start from the very back and deal damage with Xerath W Eye of Destruction and Xerath R Rite of the Arcane when your allies lock down an opponent. Xerath R Rite of the Arcane roots you in place, so secure a safe position before using it.
Milio.watch: Milio Q Ultra Mega Fire Kick knocks back and slows the first enemy it hits, so keep your distance to avoid being hit while charging Xerath Q Arcanopulse in a slowed state. When Milio W Cozy Campfire is active and extends the enemy marksman's range, delay fighting the frontline.

Morgana.build: Buy Null-Magic Mantle to survive early, then choose Mercury's Treads. Morgana's main damage is magic, and Xerath has low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first.
