Morgana.combo: After Morgana E Black Shield is down, stun her with Xerath E Shocking Orb, hit the center of Xerath W Eye of Destruction, then fire Xerath Q Arcanopulse. If Xerath E Shocking Orb misses, don't continue the combo; save your mana.
Morgana.escape: When Morgana Q Dark Binding misses and Morgana E Black Shield is down, look for a chance to stun her with Xerath E Shocking Orb. Morgana has no ability to create distance on her own, but Xerath also has no ability to escape, so stay outside the range of Morgana R Soul Shackles.
Morgana.fight: For poke, slow her by hitting the center of Xerath W Eye of Destruction, then fire Xerath Q Arcanopulse. When Morgana Q Dark Binding misses and Morgana E Black Shield is down, look for a chance to stun her with Xerath E Shocking Orb. Xerath has no ability to escape on his own, so keep your distance.
Morgana.laning: Poke with Xerath Q Arcanopulse from behind minions, and don't push the lane unnecessarily. If you need to push, secure river vision first. To save mana, cancel Xerath Q Arcanopulse when your angle is off, and use Xerath P Mana Surge with a basic attack when it's safe.
Morgana.phase: Late in the game, a positioning mistake can get you caught immediately, so fight safely from the backline.
Morgana.teamfight: Xerath should start from the very back and deal damage with Xerath W Eye of Destruction and Xerath R Rite of the Arcane after his allies lock down an opponent. Xerath R Rite of the Arcane roots you in place, so secure a safe position before using it. Save Xerath E Shocking Orb to stop enemies who get on top of you.
Morgana.watch: Dodge Morgana Q Dark Binding by keeping minions between you and her. If it hits, Morgana W Tormented Shadow and follow-up attacks will follow, so don't step back onto the pool when your health is low. If Morgana R Soul Shackles catches you, get outside its range before the stun triggers.

Naafiri.build: Buy Cloth Armor early to survive, then choose Plated Steelcaps. Naafiri's main damage is physical and Xerath has low armor, so build armor first. Get Zhonya's Hourglass early as well to prepare for her engage.
Naafiri.combo: Stun Naafiri's engage with Xerath E Shocking Orb, hit the center of Xerath W Eye of Destruction, then follow with Xerath Q Arcanopulse. If Xerath E Shocking Orb misses, don't continue the combo; save your mana. Before channeling Xerath R Rite of the Arcane from a safe position, lock her down first with Xerath E Shocking Orb or Xerath W Eye of Destruction.
Naafiri.escape: Right after Naafiri E Eviscerate is your chance to clear the pack and counterattack. Naafiri can chain several movement abilities, so don't move in deep just because one is down. In particular, look for a chance to stun her with Xerath E Shocking Orb before Naafiri R Hounds' Pursuit comes back.
Naafiri.fight: Right after Naafiri E Eviscerate, clear the revived pack with an area-of-effect ability such as Xerath R Rite of the Arcane, then counterattack. For poke that isn't a kill attempt, slow her with Xerath W Eye of Destruction, then hit Xerath Q Arcanopulse. If Naafiri still has a dash available, don't spend Xerath E Shocking Orb first.
Naafiri.laning: Use your range advantage to farm and poke from behind minions, and don't give Naafiri an angle to close in with Naafiri E Eviscerate. Don't push the lane unnecessarily; if you need to, secure river vision first. To save mana, use Xerath Q Arcanopulse only when you have a clear angle to hit, and cancel it if your angle is off.
Naafiri.phase: Early on, Xerath is fragile and spends a lot of mana, so poke sparingly from a safe distance. Late in the game, stay grouped with your allies so a positioning mistake doesn't let the enemy engage on you.
Naafiri.teamfight: Start from the very back and deal damage with Xerath W Eye of Destruction and Xerath R Rite of the Arcane after your allies lock down an opponent. Save Xerath E Shocking Orb to stop Naafiri if she gets onto your backline. If Naafiri R Hounds' Pursuit is available, don't travel alone. Retreat immediately after an ally dies so you aren't picked off next.
Naafiri.watch: If Naafiri Q Darkin Daggers hits you once, create distance until the bleed ends to avoid the second hit. Naafiri E Eviscerate and Naafiri R Hounds' Pursuit are dashes, so save Xerath E Shocking Orb to stop her engage. Naafiri W The Call of the Pack makes her untargetable briefly, so attack after it ends.

Nami.build: Early on, buy Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Nami's damage is mostly magic and Xerath has relatively low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first.
Nami.combo: After Nami Q Aqua Prison misses, if you see a chance for a kill, stun her with Xerath E Shocking Orb, hit the center of Xerath W Eye of Destruction, then fire Xerath Q Arcanopulse. If Xerath E Shocking Orb misses, don't continue the combo; save your mana. For light poke, slow her first with Xerath W Eye of Destruction, then fire Xerath Q Arcanopulse.
Nami.escape: Right after Nami Q Aqua Prison misses is your chance to close the distance. If Nami R Tidal Wave has also passed and you have an angle that minions won't block, stun her with Xerath E Shocking Orb and attack. Xerath has no ability to escape on his own, so keep your distance while enemy crowd control is available.
Nami.fight: Right after Nami Q Aqua Prison misses, slow her with Xerath W Eye of Destruction and land Xerath Q Arcanopulse. Nami has no mobility, so secure vision and look for an angle toward her, but when using Xerath E Shocking Orb, choose a position where minions won't block it.
Nami.laning: Use your range advantage to poke Nami with Xerath Q Arcanopulse from behind minions, and don't push the lane unnecessarily. Mana is scarce early, so cast only when you have a clear angle to hit and cancel if your angle is off. If you need to push the lane, secure river vision first.
Nami.phase: Late in the game, it's easy to get caught after a positioning mistake, so keep a safe distance.
Nami.teamfight: Start from the very back, and deal damage with Xerath W Eye of Destruction and Xerath R Rite of the Arcane after your allies lock down an opponent. You can move during Xerath R Rite of the Arcane, so secure a safe position before using it. Save Xerath E Shocking Orb to stop an opponent who gets on top of you.
Nami.watch: Nami Q Aqua Prison stuns you, and getting hit by Nami R Tidal Wave makes it easy to get hit by the follow-up combo as well. When you see either ability coming, walk sideways to dodge. Don't fight head-on against a target affected by Nami E Tidecaller's Blessing; resume poking after its duration ends.

Nautilus.build: Early on, buy Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Build magic resistance first, accounting for Nautilus's main damage and Xerath's low magic resistance.
Nautilus.combo: For poke, slow him by hitting the center of Xerath W Eye of Destruction, then land Xerath Q Arcanopulse. If Nautilus Q Dredge Line is down and you have a chance for a kill, stun him with Xerath E Shocking Orb, hit the center of Xerath W Eye of Destruction during the stun, then use Xerath Q Arcanopulse. If Xerath E Shocking Orb misses, don't continue the combo; save your mana.
Nautilus.escape: Right after Nautilus Q Dredge Line misses is your window to step forward and trade. If you hit Xerath E Shocking Orb then, Nautilus will have a hard time dodging Xerath Q Arcanopulse and Xerath W Eye of Destruction. Finish the trade outside his basic attack range so you don't get rooted by Nautilus P Staggering Blow.
Nautilus.fight: If Nautilus Q Dredge Line misses, keep your distance, slow him with Xerath W Eye of Destruction, then trade with Xerath Q Arcanopulse. If Nautilus engages, stop him with your saved Xerath E Shocking Orb and retreat.
Nautilus.laning: Poke with Xerath Q Arcanopulse from behind minions, and don't push the lane unnecessarily. Xerath E Shocking Orb is blocked by minions, so look for an angle where the minion line won't overlap when Nautilus engages. To save mana, cancel Xerath Q Arcanopulse if you don't have a clear angle to hit. If you need to push the lane, secure river vision first.
Nautilus.phase: Early on, Xerath is fragile and short on mana, so focus on dodging Nautilus Q Dredge Line. Late in the game, getting caught by Nautilus's engage after one positioning mistake is dangerous, so prioritize a safe distance.
Nautilus.teamfight: Xerath should start from the backline and avoid standing in line with allies along the path of Nautilus R Depth Charge. After your allies lock down an opponent, deal damage with Xerath W Eye of Destruction and Xerath R Rite of the Arcane, but channel your ultimate only after securing a safe position. Save Xerath E Shocking Orb to stop Nautilus when he engages on you.
Nautilus.watch: Nautilus Q Dredge Line leads into an engage and stun, so dodge it with minions between you and him. After he hooks you, Nautilus P Staggering Blow's root and Nautilus R Depth Charge's crowd control can follow, so stay outside his basic attack range too. When Nautilus R Depth Charge is available, don't stand in line with your allies along the engage path.

Orianna.build: Buy a Null-Magic Mantle first to survive the early game. Orianna’s main damage is magic, so build magic resistance and choose Mercury’s Treads.
Orianna.combo: For a kill, stun Orianna with Xerath E Shocking Orb from an angle where minions won’t block it, then hit the center of Xerath W Eye of Destruction and follow with Xerath Q Arcanopulse. If Xerath E Shocking Orb misses, don’t continue the combo; save your mana. For light poke, slow her first with Xerath W Eye of Destruction, then fire Xerath Q Arcanopulse.
Orianna.escape: Look for a chance to advance when Orianna W Command: Dissonance and Orianna R Command: Shockwave have been used and the ball isn’t nearby. Orianna has no ability to create distance on her own, so hitting Xerath E Shocking Orb from an angle where minions won’t block it makes it easy to follow up with attacks.
Orianna.fight: Look to trade right after Orianna Q Command: Attack moves the ball away from her, when she has no sustained defensive stats from Orianna E Command: Protect. Hit the center of Xerath W Eye of Destruction to slow her, then fire Xerath Q Arcanopulse. Avoid fights where Orianna P Clockwork Windup lets her land repeated empowered basic attacks.
Orianna.laning: Poke from behind minions with Xerath Q Arcanopulse’s range, but don’t push the lane without a reason. Look for moments when Orianna steps forward to last-hit minions, and cancel Xerath Q Arcanopulse to save mana if the angle is off. If you need to push, secure river vision first.
Orianna.phase: Positioning is especially important in the late game, so attack from a safe distance.
Orianna.teamfight: Start from the back, watch the ball rather than Orianna herself, and avoid places where Orianna R Command: Shockwave could pull you in. After your allies lock down an opponent, deal damage with Xerath W Eye of Destruction and Xerath R Rite of the Arcane, and save Xerath E Shocking Orb to stop enemies who get on top of you. You can’t move while casting Xerath R Rite of the Arcane, so secure a safe position first.
Orianna.watch: Watch the ball’s position after Orianna Q Command: Attack moves it, and don’t stand near it. Near the ball, beware the slow from Orianna W Command: Dissonance and the forced displacement from Orianna R Command: Shockwave. Avoid that area even while charging Xerath Q Arcanopulse.

Pantheon.build: Buy Cloth Armor early to survive and choose Plated Steelcaps. Pantheon’s main damage is physical, and Xerath has low armor, so build armor first.
Pantheon.combo: If you interrupt Pantheon’s engage with Xerath E Shocking Orb and stun him, hit the center of Xerath W Eye of Destruction, then follow with Xerath Q Arcanopulse. If Xerath E Shocking Orb misses, don’t continue the combo; save your mana. For poke when you don’t have a kill opportunity, slow him with Xerath W Eye of Destruction, then fire Xerath Q Arcanopulse.
Pantheon.escape: Don’t go in just because Pantheon W Shield Vault is down; wait until Pantheon R Grand Starfall is down too. Pantheon will have a hard time escaping if you hit him with Xerath E Shocking Orb before Pantheon R Grand Starfall comes back up.
Pantheon.fight: Avoid trading blows early, and poke from outside Pantheon W Shield Vault’s range while watching for it. When poking, slow him with Xerath W Eye of Destruction, then hit him with Xerath Q Arcanopulse. Save Xerath E Shocking Orb to interrupt Pantheon’s dash.
Pantheon.laning: Stand with minions between you and Pantheon to reduce poke damage from Pantheon Q Comet Spear, and use Xerath Q Arcanopulse against Pantheon when he steps forward to farm. Don’t push the lane without a reason; if you need to push, secure river vision first. Save mana and poke only when you have a clear hit, and use basic attacks to trigger Xerath P Mana Surge when it’s safe.
Pantheon.phase: Pantheon’s influence falls off in the late game, but Xerath is also at risk if he mispositions and gets engaged on, so keep a safe distance.
Pantheon.teamfight: Start from the back and deal damage with Xerath W Eye of Destruction and Xerath R Rite of the Arcane when your allies lock down an opponent. Save Xerath E Shocking Orb to interrupt Pantheon when he gets on top of you. You can’t move while casting Xerath R Rite of the Arcane, so secure a safe position, and move outside the landing area when you see the warning for Pantheon R Grand Starfall.
Pantheon.watch: Pantheon W Shield Vault is a targeted ability that stuns, so stay outside its range; if he approaches, interrupt his engage with Xerath E Shocking Orb. While Pantheon E Aegis Assault is active, wait to attack him from the front. When you see the landing warning for Pantheon R Grand Starfall, walk out of its area.

Pyke.build: In the early game, buy Cloth Armor first and choose Plated Steelcaps. Pyke’s damage is mostly physical, so prioritize armor, but also build total health because Pyke stacks armor penetration and has an execute threshold. Get Zhonya’s Hourglass earlier to prepare for his engage.
Pyke.combo: If Xerath E Shocking Orb stuns Pyke, hit the center of Xerath W Eye of Destruction, then fire Xerath Q Arcanopulse. If Xerath E Shocking Orb misses, don’t continue the combo; save your mana. For poke without a kill opportunity, slow him first with Xerath W Eye of Destruction, then follow with Xerath Q Arcanopulse.
Pyke.escape: When Pyke E Phantom Undertow is down, you have a chance to attack, but don’t rush in if Pyke R Death From Below is still available. Wait until you’ve confirmed Pyke R Death From Below is down, then stun Pyke with Xerath E Shocking Orb and combo him.
Pyke.fight: Poke from outside his range and save Xerath E Shocking Orb to interrupt Pyke’s engage. After sidestepping Pyke E Phantom Undertow, if Pyke R Death From Below is also down, stun him with Xerath E Shocking Orb and attack. Don’t charge Xerath Q Arcanopulse for long when Pyke is close.
Pyke.laning: Poke with Xerath Q Arcanopulse from behind minions, but don’t push the lane without a reason. Xerath runs low on mana early, so cancel Xerath Q Arcanopulse when there’s no chance to hit, and use basic attacks to trigger Xerath P Mana Surge when it’s safe. If Pyke backs off to heal, use wards or maintain vision to stop Pyke P Gift of the Drowned Ones from healing him.
Pyke.phase: In the late game, a positioning mistake can put you in danger, so watch for Pyke’s engage and stay in a safe position.
Pyke.teamfight: Start from the back. After your allies lock down an opponent, deal damage with Xerath W Eye of Destruction and Xerath R Rite of the Arcane. Save Xerath E Shocking Orb to interrupt Pyke’s engage, and use Xerath R Rite of the Arcane only after securing a safe position because you can’t move while casting it. Spread out from low-health allies to reduce the risk of Pyke R Death From Below chaining.
Pyke.watch: If Pyke Q Bone Skewer pulls you or Pyke E Phantom Undertow stuns you, Xerath is easy to hit again because he has no escape ability. Move to the side of the path left by Pyke E Phantom Undertow, and retreat toward allies or a turret when you see the shark shadow from Pyke W Ghostwater Dive. Beware Pyke R Death From Below and don’t stand near low-health allies.

Qiyana.build: Qiyana’s main damage is physical and Xerath has low armor, so buy Cloth Armor first and choose Plated Steelcaps. Get Zhonya’s Hourglass early to prepare for being caught when Xerath E Shocking Orb is down or while casting Xerath R Rite of the Arcane.
Qiyana.combo: For a kill, stun her with Xerath E Shocking Orb, hit the center of Xerath W Eye of Destruction, and finish with Xerath Q Arcanopulse. If Xerath E Shocking Orb misses, don’t continue the combo; save your mana. For light poke, slow her first with Xerath W Eye of Destruction, then fire Xerath Q Arcanopulse.
Qiyana.escape: Don’t rush in when only Qiyana W Terrashape is down, because Qiyana can escape with her remaining Qiyana E Audacity. If Qiyana uses both mobility abilities, especially while Qiyana E Audacity is still down, catch her with Xerath E Shocking Orb and attack.
Qiyana.fight: Keep your distance while Qiyana W Terrashape and Qiyana E Audacity are available, and save Xerath E Shocking Orb to interrupt her engage. If Qiyana uses both mobility abilities and remains in front of you, stun her with Xerath E Shocking Orb and counterattack.
Qiyana.laning: Use your range advantage to poke from behind minions, but don’t push the lane without a reason. When Qiyana steps forward to farm, slow her with Xerath W Eye of Destruction and hit her with Xerath Q Arcanopulse. Xerath E Shocking Orb is blocked by minions, so position at an angle that doesn’t overlap with minions to catch Qiyana’s engage.
Qiyana.phase: Early on, Xerath uses a lot of mana and is fragile, so conserve poke and keep your distance. Mid game is when Qiyana is strongest, and Xerath is also strong once he has ability power and mana, so let her engage pass and then counterattack. Qiyana’s relative strength falls off late, but Xerath is still at risk after a single positioning mistake, so move with allies and stay away from terrain.
Qiyana.teamfight: Start from the back and save Xerath E Shocking Orb to interrupt Qiyana when she gets on top of you. After your allies lock down an opponent, deal damage with Xerath W Eye of Destruction and Xerath R Rite of the Arcane. You can’t move while casting Xerath R Rite of the Arcane, so secure a safe position, and when grouping with allies, stay away from terrain where Qiyana R Supreme Display of Talent could explode.
Qiyana.watch: If Qiyana closes the distance with Qiyana E Audacity and Qiyana W Terrashape, Xerath has a hard time avoiding her follow-up attacks because he has no mobility. If Qiyana approaches holding the river element, move outside the root range of Qiyana Q Elemental Wrath / Edge of Ixtal. If she disappears while holding the brush element, move into your allies’ vision. Qiyana R Supreme Display of Talent explodes when it hits terrain, so don’t stand with your back to a wall or face her in a narrow river passage.

Rakan.build: In the early game, buy a Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury’s Treads. Rakan’s damage is mostly magic, so prioritize magic resistance.
Rakan.combo: When Rakan W Grand Entrance is down and you have a chance to kill Rakan, stun him with Xerath E Shocking Orb, hit the center of Xerath W Eye of Destruction, then fire Xerath Q Arcanopulse. If Xerath E Shocking Orb misses, don’t continue the combo; save your mana.
Rakan.escape: The moment after you make Rakan use Rakan W Grand Entrance is your chance to close the distance or kill him. In particular, when Rakan is alone and separated from his allies, he can’t use Rakan E Battle Dance to reach an ally, so look for an angle to hit him with Xerath E Shocking Orb.
Rakan.fight: Trade immediately after Rakan P Fey Feathers’ shield is removed. For poke without a kill opportunity, hit the center of Xerath W Eye of Destruction to slow him, then follow with Xerath Q Arcanopulse. If Rakan still has his dash, save Xerath E Shocking Orb to interrupt his engage.
Rakan.laning: Poke with Xerath Q Arcanopulse from behind minions and don’t push the lane without a reason. If Rakan uses Rakan W Grand Entrance, dodge sideways from the landing point and fire Xerath E Shocking Orb from an angle where minions won’t block it. Save mana and fire Xerath Q Arcanopulse only when the opponent is in a position to be hit. If you need to push the lane, secure river vision first.
Rakan.phase: In the late game, a positioning mistake can get you caught by Rakan’s engage, so secure a safe position first.
Rakan.teamfight: Start from the back and stand in a line so Rakan R The Quickness doesn’t catch multiple people. Watch Rakan W Grand Entrance’s landing point and sidestep; if minions won’t block it, interrupt Rakan with Xerath E Shocking Orb. After your allies lock down an opponent, deal damage with Xerath W Eye of Destruction and Xerath R Rite of the Arcane, but secure a safe position before casting Xerath R Rite of the Arcane.
Rakan.watch: Rakan W Grand Entrance’s landing point is visible ahead of time, so sidestep when Rakan starts moving. When Rakan R The Quickness is active, don’t try to dodge by walking; use terrain to keep him apart or interrupt him with Xerath E Shocking Orb before he reaches you.

Rell.build: In the early game, buy a Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury’s Treads. Rell’s main damage is magic and Xerath has low magic resistance, so prioritize magic resistance. Tenacity also matters for Xerath, who can easily be chained by Rell’s crowd control.
Rell.combo: If Rell’s mobility abilities are down and you can hit her with Xerath E Shocking Orb, stun her with E, hit the center of Xerath W Eye of Destruction, and follow with Xerath Q Arcanopulse. If E misses, stop the combo and save your mana. For light poke, apply the slow from Xerath W Eye of Destruction first, then fire Xerath Q Arcanopulse.
Rell.escape: Don’t go in just because Rell W Ferromancy: Crash Down is down. While Rell E Full Tilt is also down and hasn’t come back up, stun her with Xerath E Shocking Orb to make it hard for her to escape.
Rell.fight: From outside the range of Rell W Ferromancy: Crash Down, slow her with Xerath W Eye of Destruction, then poke with Xerath Q Arcanopulse. When Rell can dash in, save Xerath E Shocking Orb for self-defense. Create distance right after Rell uses Rell W Ferromancy: Crash Down, and look for an opportunity to attack after Rell E Full Tilt is also down.
Rell.laning: Poke with Xerath Q Arcanopulse from behind minions, but don’t push the lane without a reason. Rell has low magic resistance early and no way to heal in lane, so chip away whenever you can hit from outside her engage range. Xerath uses a lot of mana early, so don’t fire Xerath Q Arcanopulse if the angle is off; cancel it instead. If you need to push, secure river vision first.
Rell.phase: Early on, Xerath uses a lot of mana and is fragile, so keep your distance and poke sparingly. Rell has low magic resistance early and no way to heal, so if you keep landing hits while avoiding her engage, you can force her to recall first. In the late game, a single positioning mistake can get you caught, so fight from a safe distance.
Rell.teamfight: Start from the back and spread out from your allies so Rell R Magnet Storm doesn’t pull you in together. After your allies lock down an opponent, deal damage with Xerath W Eye of Destruction and Xerath R Rite of the Arcane, and save Xerath E Shocking Orb to interrupt Rell’s engage on you. You can’t move while casting Xerath R Rite of the Arcane, so use it only after securing a safe position outside Rell’s engage range.
Rell.watch: Rell W Ferromancy: Crash Down dashes a short distance and knocks you up, so stay outside its range and interrupt her engage with Xerath E Shocking Orb if she comes in. If Rell and an ally both speed up, that signals Rell E Full Tilt is preparing an engage, so stop trading and back away. Dodge Rell Q Shattering Strike sideways, and spread out from allies so Rell R Magnet Storm doesn’t pull multiple people in.

Renata.build: In the early game, buy a Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury’s Treads. Renata Glasc’s damage is mostly magic, so Xerath should prioritize magic resistance.
Renata.combo: The reliable combo is to stun her with Xerath E Shocking Orb, hit the center of Xerath W Eye of Destruction, then fire Xerath Q Arcanopulse. Renata Glasc has no mobility ability, so look for this combo when Renata Glasc Q Handshake is down. If minions block Xerath E Shocking Orb or it misses, stop the combo and save your mana.
Renata.escape: Engage when Renata Glasc Q Handshake is down and you can avoid the threat of Renata Glasc R Hostile Takeover. Until then, keep your distance behind minions and save Xerath E Shocking Orb for self-defense.
Renata.fight: For trades without a kill opportunity, hit the center of Xerath W Eye of Destruction to slow her, then fire Xerath Q Arcanopulse. Renata Glasc has no mobility ability, so when Renata Glasc Q Handshake is down and you get a chance to close the distance, stun her with Xerath E Shocking Orb and attack. If Xerath E Shocking Orb misses, don’t spend mana on a follow-up combo.
Renata.laning: Poke Renata Glasc with Xerath Q Arcanopulse from behind minions, and don’t push the lane without a reason. Cancel Xerath Q Arcanopulse to save mana when there’s no good opportunity to poke, and use basic attacks to trigger Xerath P Mana Surge when it’s safe. If you need to push, secure river vision first.
Renata.phase: In the late game, it’s easy to get caught after a positioning mistake, so fight from a safe distance.
Renata.teamfight: Start from the back and spread out from allies while Renata Glasc R Hostile Takeover is available. When your allies lock down an opponent, deal damage with Xerath W Eye of Destruction and Xerath R Rite of the Arcane, but secure a safe position before casting R. Save Xerath E Shocking Orb to interrupt enemies who get on top of you.
Renata.watch: If Renata Glasc Q Handshake hits you, you are rooted and can then be thrown, so dodge from behind minions or your frontline. Renata Glasc E Loyalty Program travels in a straight line and deals damage and slows, so sidestep it. If Renata Glasc R Hostile Takeover hits you, you lose control and attack nearby allies, so spread out from allies while R is available. If you kill an enemy affected by Renata Glasc W Bailout, retreat with your allies so that enemy can’t contribute to a takedown.

Ryze.build: In the early game, buy Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury’s Treads for your boots. Ryze’s main damage is magic, and Xerath has relatively low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first.
Ryze.combo: Stun Ryze with Xerath E Shocking Orb, hit the center of Xerath W Eye of Destruction, then follow with Xerath Q Arcanopulse. If E misses, don’t continue the combo; save your mana. For regular poke, slow him with W, then fire Q.
Ryze.escape: Dodge Ryze E Spell Flux, and if Ryze W Rune Prison is also down, start your combo by stunning him with Xerath E Shocking Orb.
Ryze.fight: For trades that aren’t kill attempts, slow Ryze with Xerath W Eye of Destruction, then hit him with Xerath Q Arcanopulse.
Ryze.laning: Don’t push the lane without a reason; if you have to, secure river vision first. If your Q angle is off, cancel it instead of firing.
Ryze.phase: In the late game, a poor position makes you easy to catch, so keep a safe distance.
Ryze.teamfight: Start from the back line. After your allies lock down Ryze, deal damage with Xerath W Eye of Destruction and Xerath R Rite of the Arcane. Save Xerath E Shocking Orb to stop enemies who get on top of you.
Ryze.watch: When Ryze E Spell Flux marks you, Ryze W Rune Prison roots you and Ryze Q Overload is empowered, so dodge E first. If the mark hits you, move away from your allies and keep your distance until it disappears.

Seraphine.build: In the early game, buy Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury’s Treads for your boots. Seraphine’s damage is mainly magic, and Xerath has relatively low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first.
Seraphine.combo: For a kill attempt, stun Seraphine with Xerath E Shocking Orb from an angle where minions won’t block it, hit the center of Xerath W Eye of Destruction, then follow with Xerath Q Arcanopulse. If Xerath E Shocking Orb misses, don’t continue the combo; save your mana.
Seraphine.escape: When Seraphine E Beat Drop is down, you have a chance to approach and trade. Seraphine has no mobility, so after closing the gap, she’ll have trouble escaping if Xerath E Shocking Orb hits. Xerath also has no ability to escape on his own, so don’t force an engage while Seraphine E Beat Drop is available.
Seraphine.fight: You have a chance to trade right after Seraphine E Beat Drop is down. If it isn’t a kill attempt, slow her with Xerath W Eye of Destruction, then hit her with Xerath Q Arcanopulse. Seraphine has trouble using an empowered basic attack when she’s alone, so look for that moment while managing your distance to avoid getting caught.
Seraphine.laning: From behind your minions, poke with Xerath Q Arcanopulse when Seraphine steps forward or backs away. If your angle is off, cancel instead of firing. Don’t push the lane without a reason; if you have to, secure river vision first.
Seraphine.phase: Early on, Xerath is fragile and uses a lot of mana, so limit how often you poke. In the late game, even one poor positioning choice can be dangerous, so keep a safe distance.
Seraphine.teamfight: Start from the back line and spread out to either side so Seraphine R Encore doesn’t extend through your allies. After your allies lock down an enemy, deal damage with Xerath W Eye of Destruction and Xerath R Rite of the Arcane. You can move while using Xerath R Rite of the Arcane, so secure a safe position first, and save Xerath E Shocking Orb to stop enemies who get on top of you.
Seraphine.watch: Seraphine E Beat Drop roots slowed targets and stuns immobilized targets. If you’re slowed, first get out of the straight line in front of Seraphine. In teamfights, Seraphine R Encore gains range each time it passes through an allied champion, so spread out to either side of your allies.

Sona.build: Buy Null-Magic Mantle early to withstand Sona’s main magic damage, and choose Mercury’s Treads for your boots. Xerath’s magic damage is effective against Sona’s low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first.
Sona.combo: For a kill attempt where you can prevent Sona from escaping with Sona E Song of Celerity, stun her with Xerath E Shocking Orb, hit the center of Xerath W Eye of Destruction, then follow with Xerath Q Arcanopulse. If Xerath E Shocking Orb misses, don’t continue the combo; save your mana.
Sona.escape: Look for a chance to catch Sona after Sona R Crescendo is down and before she can create distance with Sona E Song of Celerity. If Xerath E Shocking Orb hits when Sona steps forward, she can’t escape with Sona E Song of Celerity alone.
Sona.fight: Look to trade when Sona steps forward to share her aura. If it isn’t a kill attempt, slow her with Xerath W Eye of Destruction, then hit her with Xerath Q Arcanopulse. If she tries to escape with Sona E Song of Celerity, catch her with the stun from Xerath E Shocking Orb.
Sona.laning: Use Xerath Q Arcanopulse from behind your minions, and don’t push the lane without a reason. If you have to push, secure river vision first, and use basic attacks to trigger Xerath P Mana Surge when it’s safe.
Sona.phase: In the late game, Sona gets stronger with growth stacks and auras, so Xerath should stay in a safe position.
Sona.teamfight: Xerath should start from the back line and spread out to either side so your allies don’t all get hit by Sona R Crescendo. When your allies lock down an enemy, deal damage with Xerath W Eye of Destruction and Xerath R Rite of the Arcane, and save Xerath E Shocking Orb to stop enemies who get on top of you. If Sona is separated from her allies, her aura won’t reach them, so disrupt their formation. Prepare for extended teamfights by making sure your team has at least one Grievous Wounds item.
Sona.watch: Sona R Crescendo stuns everyone it hits in a straight line, so don’t stand in a line with your allies when Sona steps forward. If Sona suddenly gets within basic attack range, watch out for her empowered attack from Sona P Power Chord and create distance in advance.

Soraka.build: In the early game, buy Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury’s Treads for your boots. Soraka’s damage is magic, so prioritize magic resistance. If her healing extends the fight, consider Grievous Wounds next.
Soraka.combo: When you’re sure you can kill Soraka, stun her with Xerath E Shocking Orb, hit the center of Xerath W Eye of Destruction, then fire Xerath Q Arcanopulse. Xerath E Shocking Orb is blocked by minions, so use it from an angle that doesn’t line up with them. If the stun misses, don’t continue the combo; save your mana.
Soraka.escape: Right after Soraka E Equinox is down, you have a chance to close the gap. Move before stepping into the silence area, and hit her with Xerath E Shocking Orb to lock her down when she can’t escape with mobility.
Soraka.fight: For poke that isn’t a kill attempt, hit the center of Xerath W Eye of Destruction to slow the target, then follow with Xerath Q Arcanopulse. While dodging Soraka Q Starcall, pressure an allied marksman to make Soraka spend Soraka W Astral Infusion and lose health. Look for an angle to hit Xerath E Shocking Orb when Soraka E Equinox is down.
Soraka.laning: Use your range advantage to poke with Xerath Q Arcanopulse from behind minions, but don’t push the lane without a reason. Look for the moment Soraka steps forward or backs away, and cancel your charged Q if your angle is off to save mana. If you have to push, secure river vision first.
Soraka.phase: In the late game, a positioning mistake is fatal, so stay in the back line in a safe position.
Soraka.teamfight: Start from the back line, and if you can attack safely, target Soraka herself instead of the ally she’s healing. After your allies lock down an enemy, focus your damage with Xerath W Eye of Destruction and Xerath R Rite of the Arcane. You can’t move while using Xerath R Rite of the Arcane, so secure a safe position first, and save Xerath E Shocking Orb to stop enemies who get on top of you.
Soraka.watch: If Soraka Q Starcall hits you, Soraka heals and gains movement speed, so dodge Q Starcall while poking. In Soraka E Equinox’s area, you are silenced and can be rooted, so leave its area before stepping into it. Soraka R Wish heals allies regardless of distance, so consider whether it’s available when looking for a kill.

Sylas.build: Sylas’s damage is mainly magic, and Xerath has low magic resistance, so buy Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury’s Treads for your boots. If Sylas’s engages often catch you while Xerath E Shocking Orb is down, buy Zhonya’s Hourglass earlier.
Sylas.combo: Stun Sylas with Xerath E Shocking Orb as he engages with Sylas E Abscond / Abduct, hit the center of Xerath W Eye of Destruction, then fire Xerath Q Arcanopulse. If Xerath E Shocking Orb misses, don’t continue the combo; save your mana.
Sylas.escape: Don’t engage just because Sylas W Kingslayer is down. Look for an opportunity to hit Xerath E Shocking Orb before Sylas E Abscond / Abduct comes back up; if it hits, Sylas will have trouble escaping.
Sylas.fight: For poke that isn’t a kill attempt, hit the center of Xerath W Eye of Destruction to slow Sylas, then fire Xerath Q Arcanopulse. If Sylas engages with Sylas E Abscond / Abduct, interrupt him with Xerath E Shocking Orb, and follow with Xerath W Eye of Destruction and Xerath Q Arcanopulse only if the stun hits.
Sylas.laning: If you have to push the lane, secure river vision first, and cancel Xerath Q Arcanopulse if your angle is off.
Sylas.phase: In the late game, secure a safe position first so you don’t allow an engage.
Sylas.teamfight: Start from the back line and deal damage with Xerath W Eye of Destruction and Xerath R Rite of the Arcane after your allies lock down Sylas. Save Xerath E Shocking Orb in case Sylas engages with Sylas E Abscond / Abduct, and cast Xerath R Rite of the Arcane from a safe position.
Sylas.watch: Dodge Sylas’s chains. If Sylas Q Chain Lash grazes you, move out of its delayed explosion intersection immediately.

Syndra.build: Buy Null-Magic Mantle early to withstand her damage, and choose Mercury’s Treads for your boots. Syndra’s main damage is mostly magic, so build magic resistance first, but also consider your total health because of the true damage from Syndra W Force of Will and the execute from Syndra R Unleashed Power.
Syndra.combo: For a kill attempt, stun Syndra with Xerath E Shocking Orb, hit the center of Xerath W Eye of Destruction, then follow with Xerath Q Arcanopulse. If E misses, stop the follow-up combo to save mana. For light poke, apply W’s slow first, then fire Q.
Syndra.escape: Right after Syndra E Scatter the Weak is down, Syndra’s self-defense is weaker. Find an attack angle within range, but choose one where minions won’t block Xerath E Shocking Orb, then stun her.
Syndra.fight: Right after Syndra E Scatter the Weak is down, you have a chance to attack. Use your range advantage to slow her with Xerath W Eye of Destruction, then hit her with Xerath Q Arcanopulse. For a kill attempt, first hit Xerath E Shocking Orb from an angle where minions won’t block it, then follow up with more attacks.
Syndra.laning: Poke with Xerath Q Arcanopulse from behind minions, but don’t push the lane without a reason. Look for the moment Syndra steps forward to last-hit, and cancel a charged Q if your angle is off to save mana. If you have to push, secure river vision first.
Syndra.phase: Early on, Xerath uses a lot of mana and is fragile, so conserve your poke and farm. In the late game, a positioning mistake can get you killed instantly; reset your sense of distance when you see Syndra’s empowered ability effects.
Syndra.teamfight: Xerath should start from the back line and deal damage with Xerath W Eye of Destruction and Xerath R Rite of the Arcane when your allies lock down an enemy. You can’t move during R, so secure a safe position first, and save Xerath E Shocking Orb to stop enemies who get on top of you. Avoid areas with several Syndra Q Dark Spheres.
Syndra.watch: Move away from areas with several Syndra Q Dark Spheres, where Syndra R Unleashed Power is more dangerous.

Talon.build: In the early game, buy Cloth Armor first and choose Plated Steelcaps for your boots. Talon deals physical damage, so prioritize armor over magic resistance; if he builds lethality, get health as well. Build Zhonya’s Hourglass earlier to prepare for his engage, and add magic penetration to deal with his high magic resistance.
Talon.combo: During the window after Talon Q Noxian Diplomacy is down, stun him with Xerath E Shocking Orb, hit the center of Xerath W Eye of Destruction, then cast Xerath Q Arcanopulse. If Xerath E Shocking Orb misses, don’t continue the guaranteed combo; save your mana. For light harass, slow Talon with Xerath W Eye of Destruction, then hit him with Xerath Q Arcanopulse.
Talon.escape: Right after you make Talon use Talon Q Noxian Diplomacy is your chance to close the gap and stop him with Xerath E Shocking Orb. Talon having used Talon R Shadow Assault also gives you a window to counterattack, but don’t chase far if Talon R Shadow Assault is still available.
Talon.fight: For harass when you don’t have a kill opportunity, hit the center of Xerath W Eye of Destruction to slow Talon, then cast Xerath Q Arcanopulse. Save Xerath E Shocking Orb for when Talon uses Talon Q Noxian Diplomacy to engage.
Talon.laning: Use your range advantage to harass without pushing the wave unnecessarily. If you need to push, secure river vision first. If Talon roams, share his location and ward jungle routes; when it’s safe to push, do so to make him return to farm.
Talon.phase: Talon’s influence falls off in the late game, but Xerath is still easy to engage on if he positions poorly, so keep a safe distance.
Talon.teamfight: Start at the very back, and use Xerath E Shocking Orb to stop Talon if he dives onto your backline. Deal damage with Xerath W Eye of Destruction and Xerath R Rite of the Arcane after your allies lock down an opponent. Since you can’t move during Xerath R Rite of the Arcane, find a safe position before using it.
Talon.watch: If you’re hit by the first strike of Talon W Rake, move out of the return path to prevent him from stacking his passive. Save Xerath E Shocking Orb for Talon Q Noxian Diplomacy’s dash and engages with Talon E Assassin’s Path. When Talon R Shadow Assault is available, he can escape with its stealth and movement speed, so don’t chase recklessly.

Taric.build: In the early game, buy Null-Magic Mantle first, and choose Mercury’s Treads for your boots. Taric’s main damage is magic, so build magic resistance first.
Taric.combo: When you have a reliable hit, stun with Xerath E Shocking Orb, hit the center of Xerath W Eye of Destruction, then follow with Xerath Q Arcanopulse. If Xerath E Shocking Orb misses, don’t use the rest of the combo; save your mana. If the damage immunity from Taric R Cosmic Radiance is active, wait until it ends before using damage abilities.
Taric.escape: Right after Taric E Dazzle misses is your chance to step forward and harass. Taric has no ability to create distance on his own, so you can pin him down by landing Xerath E Shocking Orb from a safe angle. If an ally linked to him is approaching, keep your distance and watch out for their stun.
Taric.fight: Dodge Taric E Dazzle sideways to make him use it, then harass from outside its range. For a light trade, slow him with Xerath W Eye of Destruction, then hit him with Xerath Q Arcanopulse. Keep your distance so Taric can’t reach minions to land Taric P Bravado-enhanced basic attacks.
Taric.laning: Harass from behind minions with Xerath Q Arcanopulse, but don’t push the wave unnecessarily. If there’s no good angle to hit, cancel your charged Xerath Q Arcanopulse to save mana. If you need to push, secure river vision first.
Taric.phase: Xerath is fragile and mana-starved early, so avoid close trades with Taric and limit how often you harass. In the late game, position as far back as possible to avoid being engaged on.
Taric.teamfight: Start at the very back and deal damage with Xerath W Eye of Destruction and Xerath R Rite of the Arcane after your allies lock down an opponent. Don’t waste your artillery while Taric R Cosmic Radiance grants damage immunity; use Xerath E Shocking Orb to stop an approaching enemy or pin down an immune one. Attack again once the immunity ends.
Taric.watch: When you see Taric E Dazzle’s tell, move sideways to dodge it. Stop attacking while the damage immunity from Taric R Cosmic Radiance is active, and use Xerath E Shocking Orb to hold a target in place and let the duration pass.

TwistedFate.build: Buy Null-Magic Mantle first to survive the early game. Choose Mercury’s Treads for your boots and build magic resistance against Twisted Fate’s magic damage.
TwistedFate.combo: For the guaranteed combo, stun with Xerath E Shocking Orb, hit the center of Xerath W Eye of Destruction, then follow with Xerath Q Arcanopulse. If Xerath E Shocking Orb misses, don’t use follow-up abilities; save your mana. For light harass, slow Twisted Fate with Xerath W Eye of Destruction, then cast Xerath Q Arcanopulse.
TwistedFate.escape: Right after Twisted Fate uses the gold card from Twisted Fate W Pick a Card, you also have a window to attack without worrying about the stun.
TwistedFate.fight: For a trade when you don’t have a kill opportunity, hit the center of Xerath W Eye of Destruction to slow Twisted Fate, then cast Xerath Q Arcanopulse. If Twisted Fate W Pick a Card has a gold card ready, don’t enter basic attack range. When Twisted Fate R Destiny is down, landing Xerath E Shocking Orb from an angle unblocked by minions sets you up for follow-up attacks.
TwistedFate.laning: Harass with Xerath Q Arcanopulse from behind minions, and don’t push the wave unnecessarily. If you need to push, secure river vision first. Harass only when Twisted Fate steps forward to farm, and cancel Xerath Q Arcanopulse if your angle is off to save mana.
TwistedFate.phase: Mid game, when Xerath has ability power and mana, is his peak. In the late game, poor positioning can get you killed instantly, so keep a safe distance.
TwistedFate.teamfight: Start at the very back and deal damage with Xerath W Eye of Destruction and Xerath R Rite of the Arcane after your allies lock down an opponent. Save Xerath E Shocking Orb to stop enemies who get on top of you. If you see Twisted Fate use Twisted Fate R Destiny and he’s in range, interrupt his teleport with Xerath E Shocking Orb.
TwistedFate.watch: If Twisted Fate W Pick a Card has locked in a gold card, one basic attack will stun you, so stay outside his basic attack range. Reduce the damage from Twisted Fate Q Wild Cards by standing behind minions.

Veigar.build: In the early game, buy Null-Magic Mantle first to withstand Veigar’s magic damage. Choose Mercury’s Treads to prepare for Veigar E Event Horizon.
Veigar.combo: If Veigar E Event Horizon is down and minions won’t block your shot, stun him with Xerath E Shocking Orb. Then hit the center of Xerath W Eye of Destruction and cast Xerath Q Arcanopulse. If Xerath E Shocking Orb misses, stop the combo and save mana.
Veigar.escape: Once Veigar E Event Horizon is down, you have a chance to close the gap. Veigar has no ability to create distance on his own, so pin him down with Xerath E Shocking Orb then.
Veigar.fight: Once Veigar E Event Horizon is down, keep your distance, slow him with Xerath W Eye of Destruction, then harass with Xerath Q Arcanopulse. When the indicator for Veigar W Dark Matter appears, don’t stand still charging Xerath Q Arcanopulse for too long; move sideways.
Veigar.laning: Dodge Veigar Q Baleful Strike from behind minions while harassing. If you need to push, secure river vision first.
Veigar.phase: Veigar’s permanent stacks make the matchup harder in the late game, so check your positioning and whether Veigar E Event Horizon is available before fighting.
Veigar.teamfight: Start at the very back, check the position of Veigar E Event Horizon, and deal damage with Xerath W Eye of Destruction and Xerath R Rite of the Arcane after your allies lock down an opponent. Use Xerath R Rite of the Arcane from a safe position, and save Xerath E Shocking Orb to stop enemies who get on top of you.
Veigar.watch: If you’re caught in Veigar E Event Horizon, don’t cross the edge; move inside and wait for it to disappear. Watch the ground indicator for Veigar W Dark Matter and dodge sideways. If you’re below half health, get out of range of Veigar R Primordial Burst, which deals more damage based on your missing health.

Velkoz.build: In the early game, buy Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury’s Treads for your boots. Build magic resistance against Vel’Koz’s main damage, but avoid taking repeated hits first, since resistance can’t block the true damage from Vel’Koz P Organic Deconstruction and Vel’Koz R Life Form Disintegration Ray.
Velkoz.combo: If Vel’Koz E Tectonic Disruption is down and you have an angle for Xerath E Shocking Orb, stun him, hit the center of Xerath W Eye of Destruction, then cast Xerath Q Arcanopulse. Minions block Xerath E Shocking Orb, so choose an angle that doesn’t line Vel’Koz up with minions.
Velkoz.escape: Once Vel’Koz’s reliable crowd control, Vel’Koz E Tectonic Disruption, is down, you have a chance to close the gap. Vel’Koz has no mobility ability, so land Xerath E Shocking Orb then to keep him from escaping. Check that Vel’Koz E Tectonic Disruption is down, since it can knock you back if you get too close.
Velkoz.fight: For a trade without a kill opportunity, hit the center of Xerath W Eye of Destruction to slow Vel’Koz, then follow with Xerath Q Arcanopulse. If Vel’Koz E Tectonic Disruption is down, target Vel’Koz, who has no mobility ability, and pin him down with Xerath E Shocking Orb. If Xerath E Shocking Orb misses, don’t continue the combo; save mana.
Velkoz.laning: Don’t spam harass early; cast Xerath Q Arcanopulse from behind minions only when you can hit. Look for when Vel’Koz steps forward to farm or backs away, and cancel Xerath Q Arcanopulse to get the mana back if your angle is off. Don’t push the wave unnecessarily; if you need to push, secure river vision first.
Velkoz.phase: In the late game, poor positioning can get you killed instantly, so keep a safe distance.
Velkoz.teamfight: Start at the very back and deal damage with Xerath W Eye of Destruction and Xerath R Rite of the Arcane after your allies lock down an opponent. If Vel’Koz R Life Form Disintegration Ray starts, interrupt it with Xerath E Shocking Orb if possible; if you can’t, move to break line of sight. Xerath R Rite of the Arcane roots you in place, so find a safe position before using it.
Velkoz.watch: Dodge Vel’Koz Q Plasma Fission by moving toward Vel’Koz or behind the beam after it passes; don’t just move sideways, since you also need to avoid the split beams. If Vel’Koz W Void Rift and Vel’Koz E Tectonic Disruption both hit you in succession, Vel’Koz P Organic Deconstruction triggers for true damage, so retreat and let it wear off if you have stacks. When Vel’Koz R Life Form Disintegration Ray starts, prioritize interrupting it with Xerath E Shocking Orb.

Vex.build: In the early game, buy Null-Magic Mantle first. Choose Mercury’s Treads for your boots and build magic resistance against Vex’s main damage.
Vex.combo: For the guaranteed combo, stun with Xerath E Shocking Orb, hit the center of Xerath W Eye of Destruction, then follow with Xerath Q Arcanopulse. If Xerath E Shocking Orb misses, don’t use follow-up abilities; save your mana. For light harass, slow Vex first with Xerath W Eye of Destruction, then cast Xerath Q Arcanopulse.
Vex.escape: If Vex P Doom ’n Gloom has been consumed and Vex W Personal Space is also down, look to stun her with Xerath E Shocking Orb.
Vex.fight: For a trade without a kill opportunity, slow Vex with Xerath W Eye of Destruction, then hit her with Xerath Q Arcanopulse. Look for a chance to stun her with Xerath E Shocking Orb when both Vex P Doom ’n Gloom and Vex W Personal Space are down.
Vex.laning: Use your range advantage to harass with Xerath Q Arcanopulse from behind minions, and don’t push the wave unnecessarily. If you need to push, secure river vision first. You’re mana-starved early, so cancel Xerath Q Arcanopulse when you don’t have a good angle to hit, and use Xerath P Mana Surge when it’s safe.
Vex.phase: In the late game, one bad positioning choice can get you caught, so keep a safe distance.
Vex.teamfight: Start at the very back and deal damage with Xerath W Eye of Destruction and Xerath R Rite of the Arcane after your allies lock down an opponent. Save Xerath E Shocking Orb to stop Vex when she gets on top of you. If an ally marked by Vex R Shadow Surge dies shortly afterward, Vex’s ultimate resets, so low-health allies should get outside Vex’s range first.
Vex.watch: Watch out for fear while Vex P Doom ’n Gloom is active, and look for a chance to attack right after Vex uses it on the wave or to harass. Vex E Looming Darkness gets wider the farther it travels, so dodge a short distance sideways instead of blindly running backward from within its range. If you’re hit by Vex R Shadow Surge, she’ll dash in shortly, so move toward your allies immediately.

Viktor.build: In the early game, buy Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury’s Treads for your boots. Viktor deals mostly magic damage, so prioritize magic resistance.
Viktor.combo: For a kill, first hit Xerath E Shocking Orb from an angle unblocked by minions. While Viktor is stunned, hit the center of Xerath W Eye of Destruction and finish with Xerath Q Arcanopulse. If Xerath E Shocking Orb misses, don’t follow up; save your mana.
Viktor.escape: When Viktor W Gravity Field is down, you have a chance to close the gap and attack. Viktor has no dash to escape on his own, so stun him with Xerath E Shocking Orb then to keep your attack going.
Viktor.fight: When Viktor steps forward to farm, slow him first with Xerath W Eye of Destruction and hit him with Xerath Q Arcanopulse. Viktor controls the fight better at close range, so keep your range advantage in normal trades. If the distance between you has narrowed after Viktor W Gravity Field is down, stun him with Xerath E Shocking Orb to create an opportunity to attack.
Viktor.laning: Harass early, before Viktor P Glorious Evolution stacks up, but use abilities only when you have a good angle to hit to conserve Xerath’s mana. Don’t push the wave unnecessarily; harass with Xerath Q Arcanopulse from behind minions. Don’t stand in line with the wave so you can dodge Viktor E Hextech Ray.
Viktor.phase: Xerath is strongest in mid game, when he has ability power and mana, so pressure Viktor with your range and artillery. Viktor gets stronger over time, and a positioning mistake is fatal for Xerath in the late game, so keep a safe distance.
Viktor.teamfight: Xerath starts at the very back and deals damage with Xerath W Eye of Destruction and Xerath R Rite of the Arcane after his allies lock down an opponent. Save Xerath E Shocking Orb to stop enemies who get on top of you. Don’t stay in Viktor W Gravity Field, and use Xerath R Rite of the Arcane from a safe position after Viktor R Arcane Storm is down.
Viktor.watch: Viktor E Hextech Ray is a linear skillshot, so don’t stand in line with the minion wave; dodge sideways. When Viktor W Gravity Field is placed, leave it immediately rather than continuing the trade inside, and avoid the stun. Xerath R Rite of the Arcane requires you to stay in place, so use it from a safe position after Viktor R Arcane Storm is down.

Vladimir.build: Start with Null-Magic Mantle and choose Mercury’s Treads for boots. Vladimir’s main damage is magic, so build magic resistance early. If a fight drags on and his healing becomes a problem, get anti-heal next.
Vladimir.combo: First, use poke to make Vladimir use W Sanguine Pool. After the pool ends, hit Xerath E Shocking Orb from an angle where minions won’t block it. If E doesn’t hit, save your follow-up spells.
Vladimir.escape: When Vladimir W Sanguine Pool ends, you have a chance to catch him with Xerath E Shocking Orb. Vladimir moves more slowly while charging E Tides of Blood, so keep your distance and look for an angle to hit with Xerath W Eye of Destruction or Q Arcanopulse.
Vladimir.fight: For poke that isn’t a kill attempt, hit the center of Xerath W Eye of Destruction to slow Vladimir, then follow with Xerath Q Arcanopulse. Save Xerath E Shocking Orb until Vladimir W Sanguine Pool is down, then look to stun him after the pool ends. If E misses, don’t continue the combo; save your mana.
Vladimir.laning: Look to cast Xerath Q Arcanopulse when Vladimir steps forward to last-hit, and use basic attacks to trigger Xerath P Mana Surge when it’s safe. You don’t need to push the lane; if you have to, secure river vision first.
Vladimir.phase: In the late game, watch Vladimir’s scaling, and pay particular attention to Xerath’s positioning.
Vladimir.teamfight: Start from the far back, and deal damage with Xerath W Eye of Destruction and R Rite of the Arcane after an ally locks down an opponent. Save Xerath E Shocking Orb to interrupt enemies who get on top of you, and channel your immobile R only from a safe position. Don’t group with allies inside Vladimir R Hemoplague’s area; if infected, retreat until the effect ends.
Vladimir.watch: Vladimir Q Transfusion restores health, increases movement speed, and becomes empowered, so keep your distance when he steps forward to use an empowered Q. If you see Vladimir E Tides of Blood charging, put minions between you or move out of range. If you’re affected by Vladimir R Hemoplague, the damage you take increases, so step back and fight again after the effect ends.

Yasuo.build: Yasuo’s main damage is physical, and Xerath has low armor, so build armor early. Start with Cloth Armor and choose Plated Steelcaps for boots. If there are also diving assassins, get Zhonya’s Hourglass early in case Xerath E Shocking Orb is down.
Yasuo.combo: From an angle where Yasuo W Wind Wall won’t block Xerath E Shocking Orb, stun him with it, hit the center of Xerath W Eye of Destruction, then follow with Xerath Q Arcanopulse. If Xerath E Shocking Orb misses, don’t continue the combo; save your mana. For poke that isn’t a kill attempt, slow him first with Xerath W Eye of Destruction, then cast Xerath Q Arcanopulse.
Yasuo.escape: Look for an opening right after Yasuo throws his tornado, before Yasuo R Last Breath comes back up. Yasuo E Sweeping Blade comes back quickly, so don’t engage just because he used one mobility ability. Hit Xerath E Shocking Orb in conjunction with crowd control to leave him less room to escape.
Yasuo.fight: Right after Yasuo throws his tornado, he briefly has no way to knock you up, so look to trade then. First, use light poke to break Yasuo P Way of the Wanderer’s shield, then slow him by hitting the center of Xerath W Eye of Destruction, and follow with Xerath Q Arcanopulse. While Yasuo can approach with E Sweeping Blade, save Xerath E Shocking Orb to interrupt his dash.
Yasuo.laning: You don’t need to push the lane. Keep the wave thin on your side so there are fewer minions for Yasuo E Sweeping Blade to use as stepping stones. From a safe distance, poke with Xerath Q Arcanopulse when Yasuo steps forward to last-hit. Early on, conserve mana by canceling Xerath Q Arcanopulse if your aim is off, and secure river vision first if you need to push.
Yasuo.phase: Early on, Xerath is fragile and uses a lot of mana, so prioritize spacing and farming over poke. In the late game, getting caught by an engage is dangerous, so secure a safe position first.
Yasuo.teamfight: Start from the far back, and save Xerath E Shocking Orb to interrupt Yasuo’s engage with E Sweeping Blade. After an ally locks down an opponent, deal damage with Xerath W Eye of Destruction and Xerath R Rite of the Arcane. Xerath R Rite of the Arcane roots you in place, so use it only after securing a safe position.
Yasuo.watch: Yasuo E Sweeping Blade lets him dash to Xerath through minions, so avoid positions where minions can serve as stepping stones. After Yasuo Q Steel Tempest hits twice, it can knock you up with a tornado; watch for the effect and move sideways out of its line. Save Xerath E Shocking Orb, which is a projectile, when facing Yasuo W Wind Wall, and look for an angle around the wall.

Yone.build: Get Zhonya’s Hourglass early to prepare for Yone’s engage. Yone deals both physical and magic damage, so don’t rely on building only one type of resistance. Yone W Spirit Cleave deals damage based on your maximum health, so avoid choices that only add a lot of health.
Yone.combo: After Yone dives in, stun him with Xerath E Shocking Orb, then hit the center of Xerath W Eye of Destruction while he’s stunned and cast Xerath Q Arcanopulse. If Xerath E Shocking Orb misses, don’t continue the combo; save your mana.
Yone.escape: After Yone enters with E Soul Unbound, stunning him with Xerath E Shocking Orb can prevent him from returning to his body from spirit form. When moving in to retaliate, don’t assume it’s safe just because either Yone Q Mortal Steel or Yone E Soul Unbound is down. In particular, hit Xerath E Shocking Orb during the window before Yone R Fate Sealed comes back up, when his other means of moving are also down.
Yone.fight: For poke that isn’t a kill attempt, hit the center of Xerath W Eye of Destruction to slow Yone, then follow with Xerath Q Arcanopulse. When Yone can approach, don’t charge Xerath Q Arcanopulse for long; fire it quickly. Save Xerath E Shocking Orb to interrupt Yone’s dash.
Yone.laning: Poke with Xerath Q Arcanopulse from behind minions, and don’t push the lane without a reason. Back away when Yone Q Mortal Steel’s tornado is ready, and secure river vision first if you need to push.
Yone.phase: In the late game, watch for Yone’s engage, and pay extra attention to positioning and saving Xerath E Shocking Orb.
Yone.teamfight: Start from the far back in a safe position, but avoid a path where Yone R Fate Sealed can reach you alone in the back line. Keep your distance from allies so Yone W Spirit Cleave can’t hit several of you at once. When an ally locks down an opponent, deal damage with Xerath W Eye of Destruction and Xerath R Rite of the Arcane. Save Xerath E Shocking Orb to interrupt Yone if he gets on top of you.
Yone.watch: If Yone repeatedly uses Q Mortal Steel on minions to prepare his tornado, move out of range and wait for the stacks to disappear. Save Xerath E Shocking Orb to stun Yone when he dives in with E Soul Unbound, and stay out of the path of Yone R Fate Sealed.

Zed.build: Start with Cloth Armor and choose Plated Steelcaps for boots. Zed’s main damage is physical, and Xerath has low armor, so get armor early. Also get Zhonya’s Hourglass early to prepare for his engage.
Zed.combo: Interrupt Zed’s engage with Xerath E Shocking Orb to stun him, then hit the center of Xerath W Eye of Destruction while he’s stunned and cast Xerath Q Arcanopulse. If Xerath E Shocking Orb misses, don’t continue the combo; save your mana. For poke that isn’t a kill attempt, apply the slow with Xerath W Eye of Destruction first, then follow with Xerath Q Arcanopulse.
Zed.escape: Look for an opening after Zed W Living Shadow disappears or after Zed has already swapped positions with his shadow. Look for a window before Zed R Death Mark comes back up, and account for the fact that if only one of his two mobility tools is down, he can escape with the other. Hit Xerath E Shocking Orb to stun him during that window.
Zed.fight: Right after Zed uses W Living Shadow, check whether Zed R Death Mark is also down, then look to trade. When Zed can engage, save Xerath E Shocking Orb for self-defense, and if he gets close, fire Xerath Q Arcanopulse with a short charge.
Zed.laning: Use your range advantage to poke with Xerath Q Arcanopulse from behind minions, but don’t push the lane without a reason. Look for chances when Zed steps forward to last-hit, and conserve mana by canceling Xerath Q Arcanopulse if your aim is off. Secure river vision first if you need to push.
Zed.phase: In the late game, group with allies so Zed has no isolated target to pick off, and pay particular attention to Xerath’s positioning.
Zed.teamfight: Start from the far back and save Xerath E Shocking Orb to interrupt Zed if he gets on top of you. After an ally locks down an opponent, deal damage with Xerath W Eye of Destruction and Xerath R Rite of the Arcane. Xerath R Rite of the Arcane roots you in place, so secure a safe position before using it.
Zed.watch: Watch where Zed W Living Shadow’s shadow appears, and move outside the slow range of Zed E Shadow Slash. If he engages with Zed R Death Mark, stun him with Xerath E Shocking Orb to interrupt the combo he uses to build up damage before the mark pops.

Zilean.build: Start with Null-Magic Mantle and choose Mercury’s Treads for boots. Zilean deals magic damage, so build magic resistance, but tenacity is the first stat you’ll feel when caught by his bomb stun and slow.
Zilean.combo: When you can secure a kill on Zilean, stun him with Xerath E Shocking Orb, hit the center of Xerath W Eye of Destruction, then follow with Xerath Q Arcanopulse. If Xerath E Shocking Orb is blocked by minions or misses, don’t continue the combo; save your mana. For poke only, slow him with Xerath W Eye of Destruction, then cast Xerath Q Arcanopulse.
Zilean.escape: When Zilean Q Time Bomb’s combo and Zilean E Time Warp are down, you have a chance to close the distance. Zilean has no mobility spell, so stun him with Xerath E Shocking Orb from an angle where minions won’t block it, then follow with attacks.
Zilean.fight: For a trade that isn’t a kill attempt, hit the center of Xerath W Eye of Destruction to slow the target, then cast Xerath Q Arcanopulse. After dodging Zilean Q Time Bomb’s combo and Zilean E Time Warp, take an opportunity to hit Xerath E Shocking Orb from an angle where minions won’t block it. If you can wait out Zilean R Chronoshift on a target, do so before finishing them off.
Zilean.laning: However, Xerath is also low on mana and fragile at this point, so use only Xerath Q Arcanopulse when you can hit from behind minions, and don’t push the lane without a reason.
Zilean.phase: In the late game, one positioning mistake can be fatal, so stay in a safe position at the far back.

Save Xerath E Shocking Orb to interrupt enemies who get on top of you. If an enemy carry is protected by Zilean R Chronoshift, it is better to switch your target to the vulnerable Zilean himself.
Zilean.watch: If Zilean Q Time Bomb attaches twice, it stuns, so move away from allies as soon as the first bomb attaches and get outside the blast radius. If you’re caught by the slow from Zilean E Time Warp, you’re more vulnerable to the bomb combo and enemy attacks, so don’t close the distance alone. Don’t use spells while a target affected by Zilean R Chronoshift is reviving; look to attack right after they revive.

Zoe.build: Start with Null-Magic Mantle and choose Mercury’s Treads for boots. Zoe deals mostly magic damage, and Xerath has relatively low magic resistance, so build magic resistance early. If Zoe uses R Portal Jump, retaliate by aiming at the point where she’ll return. Xerath E Shocking Orb can be used to interrupt Zoe Q Paddle Star!’s retargeting or to protect yourself.

Zoe.watch: If Zoe E Sleepy Trouble Bubble hits you, sleep triggers after a short delay, leaving you vulnerable to Zoe’s follow-up attacks. If hit, use the delay to move behind a wall or ally and get out of the angle and range of Zoe Q Paddle Star!. When you see Zoe’s casting animation as she throws Q Paddle Star!, you can interrupt her retargeting with Xerath E Shocking Orb.

Even though Zyra has no mobility spell, Xerath also has no spell to escape with, so look for an angle to hit Xerath E Shocking Orb before closing the distance.

Step on Zyra’s seeds to destroy them when no spell is coming your way, and briefly retreat from areas with many grown plants. If your angle for poke is off, cancel Xerath Q Arcanopulse to save mana.

Avoid areas where Zyra has stacked plants, and use Xerath R Rite of the Arcane only after securing a safe position.
Zyra.watch: If rooted by Zyra E Grasping Roots, you can be hit by Zyra R Stranglethorns’ knock-up and plant damage as well. Move sideways at the edge of its range to dodge Zyra E Grasping Roots, and immediately walk out of the area when you see Zyra R Stranglethorns’ summon indicator. Don’t fight where her plants have gathered.
